levels.title: Scientific Computing & Reproducible Research Foundations
levels.scope: Establish the foundational research computing stack, reproducible environment management, seed determinism, experiment logging, and open-source scientific artifact standards.
levels.prereqStated: None (entry level for undergraduate researchers and beginning graduate students)

modules.name: The Research Computing Stack: Linux, Remote Servers & Shell Environments

objectives.text: - Navigate remote Linux compute servers via SSH with key-based authentication, config profiles, and persistent terminal multiplexers (tmux, screen).
- Manage background research processes with nohup, systemd user services, and process isolation tools (htop, ps, kill).
- Monitor GPU hardware metrics in real time using nvidia-smi, nvtop, and gpustat to diagnose GPU memory allocation and compute utilization.
- Write robust Bash automation scripts for parameterized batch execution, log redirection, and environment variable propagation.
- Handle data stream redirection with standard input, output, error streams, and Unix pipeline utilities (grep, awk, sed, cut).
- Automate remote file synchronization and dataset transfers between local machines and compute servers using rsync and scp.

modules.mentalModel: The research server is an experimental laboratory where tmux sessions preserve running experiments across network disconnects.
modules.tryIt: Connect to a remote compute instance, launch a long-running simulation script inside a detached tmux session, and inspect memory allocation with nvidia-smi.
modules.outcome: Operate remote Linux research environments confidently, launch persistent jobs, and diagnose GPU allocation bottlenecks.

modules.name: Reproducible Virtual Environments: Pixi, Conda, Docker & PyPI

objectives.text: - Understand the reproducibility crisis in machine learning research caused by unpinned transitive dependencies and varying CUDA runtime binaries.
- Isolate scientific Python environments using modern package managers (Pixi, uv, Conda) with locked dependency graphs.
- Compile and install C++/CUDA extensions from source within isolated environments without contaminating system libraries.
- Author multi-stage Dockerfiles optimized for deep learning research containing specific CUDA, cuDNN, and PyTorch versions.
- Mount host scratch disks and dataset directories into containers while preserving file ownership and non-root execution permissions.
- Export locked environment manifests (environment.lock.yml, pyproject.toml) to ensure identical reproduction across compute clusters.

modules.mentalModel: A research environment must be an immutable, containerized artifact so that any researcher can reproduce exact numerical results five years later.
modules.tryIt: Build a reproducible container image pinning PyTorch and CUDA runtime dependencies, mounting an external dataset volume.
modules.outcome: Eliminate dependency drift, resolve CUDA version mismatches, and package research code into containerized environments.

modules.name: Version Control for Science: Git, Submodules & Open-Source Code Release

objectives.text: - Structure research Git repositories separating core libraries, model definitions, baseline benchmarks, and exploratory scripts.
- Use feature branches and semantic Git tags to mark paper submission checkpoints, rebuttal revisions, and camera-ready milestones.
- Manage external research repositories and upstream library forks cleanly using Git submodules and subtree merges.
- Author comprehensive academic README files featuring installation commands, pretrained checkpoint links, and minimal reproduction snippets.
- Include open-source research licensing (MIT, Apache 2.0, CC-BY) and BibTeX citation blocks formatted for Google Scholar and ArXiv indexing.
- Prevent data leakage and credential exposure by strictly configuring .gitignore for checkpoints, logs, raw data, and secret keys.

modules.mentalModel: Git tags in research serve as immutable cryptographic stamps linking paper figures directly to specific commit hashes.
modules.tryIt: Create a research template repository with a structured module layout, automated linter, .gitignore, and standardized BibTeX citation header.
modules.outcome: Structure academic research repositories to meet top-tier conference artifact evaluation and reproducibility standards.

modules.name: Experiment Tracking & Artifact Management: Weights & Biases and MLflow

objectives.text: - Integrate real-time experiment tracking tools (Weights & Biases, MLflow) into iterative training loops with minimal overhead.
- Log training and validation loss curves, evaluation accuracy, gradient norms, and learning rate schedules across continuous epochs.
- Structure hierarchical configuration dictionaries tracking all hyperparameters, random seeds, dataset versions, and model architectures.
- Log multimodal research artifacts including generated validation samples, confusion matrices, and interactive attention heatmaps.
- Implement an automated checkpoint saving strategy saving best-validation models, periodic epoch states, and emergency recovery snapshots.
- Compare experiment runs across multi-dimensional parallel coordinate plots to isolate hyperparameter sensitivities and performance gains.

modules.mentalModel: An experiment tracker is a digital laboratory notebook capturing the exact relationship between configuration deltas and empirical outcomes.
modules.tryIt: Instrument a PyTorch training loop with Weights & Biases, logging scalar metrics, gradient norm histograms, and validation sample predictions.
modules.outcome: Systematically track hundreds of experimental runs, visualize metric trajectories, and maintain a centralized model registry.

modules.name: Hardware Determinism, Random Seeds & Scientific Data Loaders

objectives.text: - Identify hardware and software sources of numerical non-determinism in deep learning (CUDA atomic operations, cuDNN benchmarking, CPU threading).
- Implement deterministic initialization routines seeding Python random, NumPy, PyTorch CPU/GPU generators, and cuDNN deterministic flags.
- Understand the performance trade-offs of enabling torch.use_deterministic_algorithms() during initial prototyping versus large-scale runs.
- Build multi-worker PyTorch DataLoaders with custom worker initialization functions ensuring independent, deterministic worker random states.
- Avoid common multiprocessing pitfalls in PyTorch data loaders such as shared memory exhaustion, worker deadlocks, and duplicate augmentations.
- Implement memory-mapped dataset formats and pre-fetching pipelines (Arrow, WebDataset, HDF5) to prevent CPU data starvation during GPU training.

modules.mentalModel: True scientific reproducibility requires that rerunning a script with seed 42 produces identical bitwise loss values across epochs.
modules.tryIt: Write a deterministic seed utility function, verify that two independent training runs produce identical loss curves, and benchmark data loader throughput.
modules.outcome: Eliminate stochastic noise between runs, guarantee experimental determinism, and design high-throughput scientific data pipelines.

modules.name: Capstone Project: Reproducible Experiment Harness & Pipeline Template

objectives.text: - Design a modular, object-oriented experiment harness decoupling dataset loading, model architecture, training loop, and evaluation metrics.
- Implement structured configuration parsing with type validation and command-line overrides (Hydra, Pydantic, argparse).
- Create automated logging hooks capturing Git commit hash, environment diff, hardware specifications, and package versions at runtime start.
- Build a resilient training loop featuring automated checkpoint resumption, anomaly detection for NaN gradients, and graceful signal handling.
- Author an automated smoke-test suite verifying forward pass, backward gradient flow, and data pipeline throughput on dummy synthetic tensors.
- Package the harness into a reusable research template repository with complete documentation, container definition, and continuous integration.

notes: CAPSTONE PROJECT: Reproducible Experiment Harness & Pipeline Template

BRIEF: Build a standardized, publication-ready research scaffolding framework in PyTorch that guarantees bitwise reproducibility, tracks real-time experimental metrics, handles graceful checkpoint recovery, and exports complete environment provenance for academic code releases.
Build an experiment harness that:
- Initializes deterministic random generators across Python, NumPy, and PyTorch backends with verified seed propagation to DataLoader worker processes.
- Parses hierarchical experiment configurations via structured configuration schemas with strict type validation and runtime command-line overrides.
- Logs scalar metrics, gradient norm distributions, learning rate schedules, and validation artifacts to Weights & Biases and local disk simultaneously.
- Detects NaN/Inf loss values and exploding gradients instantly, triggering informative debug dumps with tensor activation statistics.
- Implements atomic checkpoint saving with metadata sidecars recording validation metrics, optimizer states, learning rate schedules, and Git commit hashes.
- Automatically resumes interrupted training runs from the latest checkpoint without metric duplication or data epoch leakage.
- Features a unit test suite validating gradient propagation, deterministic outputs under fixed seeds, and data pipeline memory bounds.
Deliverables:
- Modular research repository featuring decoupled datasets/, models/, training/, and configs/ directories.
- Verified Dockerfile and environment lockfile reproducing the exact runtime on any CUDA-enabled system.
- An interactive Weights & Biases dashboard comparing multiple runs with distinct seeds and hyperparameter configurations.
- Comprehensive academic README with step-by-step reproduction instructions, checkpoint links, and BibTeX citation.
modules.mentalModel: A battle-tested research harness is a scientist's primary laboratory apparatus, reducing the time from new hypothesis to empirical result from weeks to hours.
modules.tryIt: Run the experiment harness with multiple configuration overrides, simulate a mid-training process termination, and verify seamless resumption from checkpoint.
modules.outcome: You can scaffold any machine learning research project with industrial-grade scientific rigor, guaranteed reproducibility, and frictionless collaboration.

levels.title: Literature Review & Scientific Problem Formulation
levels.scope: Master the academic research methodology: discovering, analyzing, and synthesizing scientific literature, identifying open research gaps, formulating formal research questions (RQs), and constructing rigorous research proposals.

modules.name: Scientific Discovery Engines: Navigating ArXiv, Google Scholar & Semantic Scholar

objectives.text: - Query academic databases (Google Scholar, Semantic Scholar, DBLP, ArXiv) using boolean search syntax and field-specific filtering.
- Track citation graphs and follow seminal lineages forward and backward using citation trees and influence metrics.
- Discover emerging preprints and conference proceedings across premier AI/ML venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ACL, KDD).
- Set up automated research alerts and topic monitoring using ArXiv RSS feeds, Hugging Face Daily Papers, and Google Scholar keyword notifications.
- Leverage visual literature exploration tools (Connected Papers, Litmaps, ResearchRabbit) to discover co-citation clusters and derivative works.
- Filter signal from noise in daily preprint releases by evaluating author lab credibility, code availability, and benchmark claims.

modules.mentalModel: The scientific literature is a dynamic, interconnected knowledge graph; exploring citation trajectories reveals where a paradigm is heading.
modules.tryIt: Map the citation graph of a foundational paper using Connected Papers, identifying the top three foundational prior works and top three derivative extensions.
modules.outcome: Systematically discover relevant academic literature, navigate citation networks, and establish an automated daily research radar.

modules.name: Critical Paper Reading: The Three-Pass Method & Deconstructing Claims

objectives.text: - Apply Keshav’s Three-Pass Method to evaluate paper relevance, grasp central ideas, and dissect technical depth in structured increments.
- Extract the core contributions in Pass 1 by analyzing title, abstract, introduction, section headers, and conclusion within 10 minutes.
- Scrutinize figures, tables, and empirical evidence in Pass 2 to assess whether experimental data genuinely supports the stated claims.
- Execute Pass 3: mentally re-implement the paper from scratch, identifying implicit assumptions, unstated tricks, and missing proofs.
- Distinguish between theoretical guarantees, empirical heuristic findings, and unverified narrative speculation in published papers.
- Identify common paper red flags: cherry-picked qualitative examples, weak or un-tuned baselines, moving goalposts, and missing ablation studies.

modules.mentalModel: Reading a paper is an active peer review where you interrogate every claim against the empirical evidence presented.
modules.tryIt: Conduct a 3-pass review of a recent top-tier conference paper, writing a 1-page structured critique evaluating its core claims and baseline fairness.
modules.outcome: Read research papers efficiently, extract core insights rapidly, and critically evaluate the validity of scientific claims.

modules.name: Citation Management & Literature Synthesis: Zotero, BibTeX & Taxonomy Building

objectives.text: - Organize academic libraries systematically using Zotero with automatic PDF metadata extraction, tag hierarchies, and DOI lookups.
- Integrate Zotero with Overleaf and local LaTeX environments via Better BibTeX for automated, clean citation key generation.
- Annotate papers with structured research notes linking methodology variants, benchmark scores, and theoretical limitations.
- Construct comparative literature synthesis matrices mapping related papers across problem formulations, architectures, and assumptions.
- Develop conceptual taxonomies that categorize existing approaches into clear methodological families with contrasting trade-offs.
- Write polished "Related Work" sections that tell a compelling historical narrative rather than providing a disjointed list of summaries.

modules.mentalModel: A literature survey is not a catalog of summaries; it is a structured taxonomy that exposes the boundaries of current human knowledge.
modules.tryIt: Build a 15-paper comparative synthesis table in Zotero, mapping existing methods across problem formulation, architecture, datasets, and limitations.
modules.outcome: Manage thousands of academic references effortlessly, maintain clean BibTeX registries, and synthesize literature into structured taxonomies.

modules.name: Identifying Research Gaps & Formulating Research Questions (RQs)

objectives.text: - Identify fertile research gaps: methodological oversights, untested domain transfers, computational bottlenecks, and contradictory published findings.
- Analyze the "Limitations and Future Work" sections of leading conference papers to extract candidate research directions.
- Distinguish between incremental "delta" tweaks (hyperparameter tuning) and substantial scientific gaps that yield meaningful contributions.
- Formulate precise, falsifiable Research Questions (RQ1, RQ2, RQ3) that guide the entire trajectory of an academic investigation.
- Frame research questions spanning capability (Can method X solve Y?), mechanism (Why does X outperform Y?), and trade-off (What is the cost of X?).
- Define measurable operational definitions and evaluation metrics for each research question to establish clear success criteria.

modules.mentalModel: A well-formulated research question contains its own verification metric; if you cannot measure the answer, the question is not yet scientific.
modules.tryIt: Select a sub-field of AI, identify an unaddressed limitation in recent SOTA papers, and formulate three formal, falsifiable Research Questions.
modules.outcome: Isolate high-impact research gaps from published literature and formalize rigorous, publication-grade research questions.

modules.name: Hypothesis Generation, Theoretical Framing & Feasibility Analysis

objectives.text: - Formulate primary and alternative hypotheses (H1, H0) predicting specific empirical outcomes when modifying an algorithmic component.
- Provide theoretical justification for why the proposed approach should work, grounded in computational complexity, optimization, or statistics.
- Anticipate confounding variables and failure modes that could invalidate the hypothesis under realistic experimental conditions.
- Evaluate compute feasibility: calculate GPU hours, parameter scales, and dataset storage requirements against available lab resources.
- Assess timeline feasibility: plan phased milestones from rapid toy proof-of-concept to full-scale empirical validation.
- Design early de-risking experiments (quick failure tests) that validate critical assumptions before committing major computational budgets.

modules.mentalModel: Strong research balances theoretical ambition with pragmatic de-risking; fail fast on toy problems before scaling compute.
modules.tryIt: Draft a feasibility budget for a research hypothesis, estimating required GPU hours, dataset disk footprints, and a 2-day proof-of-concept milestone.
modules.outcome: Formulate grounded research hypotheses, justify theoretical mechanisms, and establish resource-conscious experimental feasibility plans.

modules.name: Capstone Project: Comprehensive Literature Survey & Research Proposal Specification

objectives.text: - Conduct an exhaustive literature survey across 25+ papers in an active AI/ML research area, constructing a multi-dimensional taxonomy matrix.
- Articulate a compelling, well-justified research gap highlighting why existing methodologies fail under specific critical conditions.
- Define 3 formal Research Questions (RQs) with explicit hypotheses and measurable empirical criteria.
- Write a formal methodological proposal specifying the proposed model architecture, loss functions, and algorithmic enhancements.
- Design an end-to-end experimental plan detailing benchmark datasets, baseline implementations, metric definitions, and ablation grids.
- Author the complete proposal document in LaTeX using a standard conference template (NeurIPS/ICLR), complete with BibTeX bibliography.

notes: CAPSTONE PROJECT: Comprehensive Literature Survey & Research Proposal Specification

BRIEF: Author a formal academic research proposal in LaTeX following the official NeurIPS/ICLR conference format. The proposal must synthesize current literature in a chosen AI/ML subfield, identify a significant research gap, formalize falsifiable research questions, and outline a rigorous experimental validation blueprint.
Build a research proposal that:
- Surveys at least 25 peer-reviewed papers from top-tier AI/ML venues, organizing them into a structured taxonomic framework.
- Constructs a comparative analysis table evaluating prior works across assumptions, architectural choices, compute requirements, and empirical limits.
- Identifies an unaddressed scientific research gap supported by concrete citations and empirical analysis of prior limitations.
- Formulates three formal Research Questions (RQ1, RQ2, RQ3) accompanied by precise null and alternative hypotheses.
- Specifies the mathematical formulation of the proposed approach, including loss formulations, architectural modifications, and algorithmic pseudocode.
- Details the experimental blueprint: choice of benchmark datasets, competitive baseline models to reproduce, evaluation metrics, and planned ablation studies.
- Provides a detailed compute budget estimating GPU memory requirements, training wall-clock time, and a phased risk-mitigation timeline.
- Adheres strictly to conference formatting guidelines with clean vector figures, mathematical notation, and an authenticated BibTeX bibliography.
Deliverables:
- Formally compiled 6-page Research Proposal PDF formatted in LaTeX using the official NeurIPS or ICLR template.
- Comprehensive BibTeX library (.bib) containing cleanly formatted, verified citations for all referenced works.
- Markdown summary pitch slide-deck outline for presentation to a thesis advisor or research lab director.
modules.mentalModel: A research proposal is an architectural blueprint for a scientific paper; when executed thoroughly, writing the final paper is simply filling in the results.
modules.tryIt: Compile your complete literature survey and research proposal into a clean LaTeX PDF, verifying all cross-references, equations, and BibTeX citations.
modules.outcome: You can identify high-impact scientific opportunities, review academic literature critically, and formulate publication-grade research proposals.

levels.title: Research Mathematics & Statistical Hypothesis Testing
levels.scope: Master the core mathematical tools and statistical hypothesis testing methodologies required to derive machine learning models, prove convergence properties, and rigorously validate empirical claims in academic papers.

modules.name: Applied Linear Algebra: High-Dimensional Geometry & Spectral Methods

objectives.text: - Analyze geometric phenomena in high-dimensional vector spaces: the curse of dimensionality, concentration of measure, and orthogonality of random vectors.
- Compute orthogonal projections onto subspaces and derive projection matrices for dimensionality reduction and subspace clustering.
- Understand Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization, QR decomposition, and their applications in stable numerical computations.
- Compute Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and eigendecompositions of symmetric positive semi-definite kernel and covariance matrices.
- Apply the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem to determine optimal low-rank matrix approximations and bound reconstruction error.
- Analyze matrix condition numbers and spectral norms to predict numerical instability in deep linear layers and attention projections.

modules.mentalModel: High-dimensional representations concentrate on low-dimensional manifolds; spectral decompositions identify the principal axes of information.
modules.tryIt: Implement truncated SVD from scratch in NumPy, decompose a high-dimensional feature matrix, and compute the reconstruction error against theoretical bounds.
modules.outcome: Manipulate high-dimensional vector representations, analyze spectral properties of neural representations, and avoid numerical ill-conditioning.

modules.name: Matrix Calculus & Symbolic Derivations for Gradient Flow

objectives.text: - Master numerator and denominator layout conventions in matrix calculus for vector-valued and matrix-valued functions.
- Compute analytical gradients and Jacobians of composite matrix expressions (trace, determinant, quadratic forms, matrix inverses).
- Derive the backpropagation equations for standard neural network layers (linear projections, convolutions, self-attention, layer normalization).
- Compute the Hessian matrix of loss functions and analyze its eigenvalue spectrum to evaluate local curvature and saddle point geometry.
- Understand the Gauss-Newton approximation and Fisher Information Matrix in natural gradient descent and empirical optimization.
- Derive convergence rates for first-order gradient descent on L-smooth and mu-strongly convex objective functions.

modules.mentalModel: Backpropagation is symbolic tensor contraction along the edges of a computational directed acyclic graph.
modules.tryIt: Derive the exact analytical matrix gradient of the multi-head self-attention operation with respect to the Query weight matrix on paper, then verify with autograd.
modules.outcome: Derive exact mathematical gradients for custom architectural layers and analytically inspect optimization loss curvature.

modules.name: Probability Spaces, Density Estimation & Information Theory in ML

objectives.text: - Formalize probability spaces, random variables, cumulative distribution functions, and multivariate continuous density functions.
- Compute conditional expectations, law of total variance, and covariance matrices for multivariate Gaussian distributions.
- Implement maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation under Gaussian and Laplace priors.
- Calculate Shannon entropy, differential entropy, joint entropy, and conditional entropy for discrete and continuous distributions.
- Compute Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and Jensen-Shannon (JS) divergence between empirical and model distributions.
- Apply mutual information and the Information Bottleneck principle to quantify feature compression in deep neural representations.

modules.mentalModel: Information theory measures surprise and uncertainty; learning is compressing the input while preserving mutual information with the target.
modules.tryIt: Calculate the analytical KL divergence between two multivariate Gaussians, implement the formula, and verify against Monte Carlo sampling estimates.
modules.outcome: Apply formal probabilistic modeling to machine learning problems and compute information-theoretic metrics across learned representations.

modules.name: Statistical Hypothesis Testing: Parametric & Non-Parametric Significance in ML

objectives.text: - Formulate null (H0) and alternative (H1) hypotheses to evaluate whether a proposed model genuinely outperforms a baseline.
- Understand Type I (false positive) and Type II (false negative) errors, significance level alpha, and statistical power (1 - beta).
- Apply two-sample Student’s t-tests and paired t-tests when assumptions of normality and equal variance are verified.
- Identify why deep learning benchmark metrics often violate normality assumptions, necessitating non-parametric statistical tests.
objectives.group: Non-Parametric Tests for Machine Learning Benchmarks

objectives.text: - Execute the Wilcoxon signed-rank test for paired performance comparisons across multiple test benchmark datasets.
objectives.group: Non-Parametric Tests for Machine Learning Benchmarks

objectives.text: - Apply the Mann-Whitney U test and Kruskal-Wallis test for comparing multi-model distributions without assuming Gaussian distributions.
objectives.group: Non-Parametric Tests for Machine Learning Benchmarks

modules.mentalModel: A higher benchmark score without a statistical significance test is an unverified anecdote, not a scientific finding.
modules.tryIt: Run 10 random seeds for a proposed model and a baseline, test for normality using Shapiro-Wilk, and execute a Wilcoxon signed-rank test to compute the p-value.
modules.outcome: Formulate rigorous statistical hypothesis tests and select appropriate parametric or non-parametric tests for machine learning evaluations.

modules.name: Effect Sizes, Multiple Hypothesis Corrections & Bootstrap Confidence Intervals

objectives.text: - Differentiate between statistical significance (p < 0.05) and practical significance by computing Cohen’s d and Cliff’s delta effect sizes.
objectives.group: Effect Size Quantification & Multiple Testing Corrections

objectives.text: - Control the Family-Wise Error Rate (FWER) across multiple benchmark comparisons using the Bonferroni correction and Holm-Bonferroni method.
objectives.group: Effect Size Quantification & Multiple Testing Corrections

objectives.text: - Control the False Discovery Rate (FDR) in large-scale metric screening using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.
objectives.group: Effect Size Quantification & Multiple Testing Corrections

objectives.text: - Apply non-parametric bootstrap resampling to compute 95% confidence intervals for complex metrics (F1-score, BLEU, ROUGE, AUC-ROC).
- Understand stratified bootstrapping to preserve class balance across resampled evaluation test sets.
- Report evaluation results using mean, standard deviation, and confidence intervals across at least 5 to 10 independent random seeds.

modules.mentalModel: The p-value tells you if an effect exists; the effect size tells you if anyone should care; confidence intervals show your uncertainty.
modules.tryIt: Implement a bootstrap confidence interval function in Python, resample model predictions 1,000 times, and compute the 95% percentile confidence bounds.
modules.outcome: Compute effect sizes, correct for multiple hypothesis testing, and report confidence intervals adhering to top-tier empirical standards.

modules.name: Capstone Project: Statistical Significance & Experimental Power Analysis Suite

objectives.text: - Design a standalone scientific evaluation Python package that ingests raw model prediction logs across multiple seeds and benchmark splits.
objectives.group: Architecture of the Statistical Evaluation Suite

objectives.text: - Implement normality testing (Shapiro-Wilk, D’Agostino-Pearson) to automatically route data between parametric and non-parametric tests.
objectives.group: Architecture of the Statistical Evaluation Suite

objectives.text: - Integrate automated two-sample t-tests, paired t-tests, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and Mann-Whitney U tests with automated p-value reporting.
objectives.group: Architecture of the Statistical Evaluation Suite

objectives.text: - Incorporate Cohen’s d, Cliff’s delta, and non-parametric bootstrap 95% confidence interval estimation.
objectives.group: Effect Sizes, Power Analysis & Academic Reporting

objectives.group: Effect Sizes, Power Analysis & Academic Reporting

objectives.text: - Generate publication-ready LaTeX tables automatically annotating statistically significant improvements with bold markers and p-value asterisks.
objectives.group: Effect Sizes, Power Analysis & Academic Reporting

notes: CAPSTONE PROJECT: Statistical Significance & Experimental Power Analysis Suite

BRIEF: Build a modular Python library for AI/ML researchers that takes raw prediction logs and metric scores from multiple random seeds, evaluates statistical distributions, runs appropriate significance tests, computes effect sizes and bootstrap confidence intervals, and formats publication-ready LaTeX tables.
Build a statistical suite that:
- Ingests structured JSON/CSV experimental logs containing per-instance predictions and evaluation scores across multiple random seeds and models.
- Performs automated distribution diagnostics (Shapiro-Wilk normality test, Levene's test for equality of variances).
- Automatically selects and executes appropriate tests: paired/unpaired Student’s t-test, Welch’s t-test, Wilcoxon signed-rank test, or Mann-Whitney U test.
- Computes standardized effect sizes including Cohen’s d for parametric data and Cliff’s delta for non-parametric evaluation distributions.
- Applies multiple hypothesis testing corrections including Bonferroni, Holm-Bonferroni, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustments.
- Executes non-parametric stratified bootstrap resampling (1,000+ iterations) to compute 95% percentile and BCa confidence intervals.
- Conducts statistical power analysis estimating the number of experimental runs or test samples required to achieve 80% power at alpha = 0.05.
- Emits formatted LaTeX table source code with mean, standard deviation, confidence intervals, and statistical significance indicators (* p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01).
Deliverables:
- Clean, documented Python package with automated CLI (stat_eval --baseline baseline.json --candidate model.json --alpha 0.05).
- Comprehensive test suite validating statistical calculations against standard R and SciPy reference outputs.
- Example tutorial notebook demonstrating end-to-end statistical validation of a published conference benchmark comparison.
modules.mentalModel: A rigorous statistical analysis suite transforms noisy empirical experiment logs into defensible, publication-ready scientific evidence.
modules.tryIt: Run the statistical suite on multi-seed benchmark results comparing two models, producing an annotated LaTeX table with bootstrap confidence intervals.
modules.outcome: You can rigorously validate empirical machine learning results, prove statistical significance, and generate publication-grade experimental tables.

levels.title: Experimental Design & Rigorous Benchmarking
levels.scope: Master the principles of controlled empirical experimentation in machine learning: designing multi-factor ablation matrices, establishing fair baseline comparisons, hyperparameter optimization protocols, and preventing subtle evaluation leakage.

modules.name: Principles of Controlled Experiments: Independent, Dependent & Confounding Variables

objectives.text: - Formulate empirical experiments with strictly defined independent variables (architectural modifications, loss terms) and dependent variables (benchmark accuracy, throughput).
objectives.group: Scientific Experimental Control in Machine Learning

objectives.text: - Identify and isolate confounding variables that corrupt empirical claims: hidden optimizer tuning, differing learning rate warmups, and unequal token counts.
objectives.group: Scientific Experimental Control in Machine Learning

objectives.text: - Establish negative controls (random feature baselines, shuffled labels) and positive controls (oracle representations, upper-bound supervision).
objectives.group: Scientific Experimental Control in Machine Learning

objectives.text: - Enforce strict parameter-matched and compute-matched experimental controls when comparing novel architectures against baselines.
- Calculate and report total training FLOPs (using 6*N*D approximations) to guarantee that performance gains do not stem purely from scale.
- Normalize inference latency, peak GPU VRAM allocation, and memory bandwidth utilization during comparative benchmarking.

modules.mentalModel: If your model beats the baseline simply because it had 20% more parameters or trained with a better learning rate schedule, your scientific claim is invalid.
modules.tryIt: Design an experiment comparing two attention mechanisms where total parameter count, FLOP budget, and training token count are strictly matched.
modules.outcome: Structure scientifically controlled machine learning experiments that isolate genuine algorithmic contributions from confounding factors.

modules.name: Ablation Study Design: Component Isolation & Negative Controls

objectives.text: - Understand the primary purpose of an ablation study: proving that every proposed component is strictly necessary and operates as hypothesized.
objectives.group: The Anatomy of a High-Impact Ablation Study

objectives.text: - Design one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) and full factorial ablation grids that systematically remove or substitute individual algorithmic modules.
objectives.group: The Anatomy of a High-Impact Ablation Study

objectives.text: - Formulate component-level ablations: testing custom loss components, normalization layers, positional encodings, and data filtering thresholds.
objectives.group: The Anatomy of a High-Impact Ablation Study

objectives.text: - Implement random ablation baselines: replace learned modules with random projections or identity mappings to measure actual learned contribution.
- Execute feature permutation and ablation tests to verify that model performance degrades when critical input signals are corrupted.
- Structure ablation tables in scientific papers with incremental rows showing progressive performance deltas from baseline to proposed system.

modules.mentalModel: An ablation study is an empirical post-mortem showing the exact quantitative damage incurred when any piece of your innovation is removed.
modules.tryIt: Construct an ablation matrix for a model with three new components (loss penalty, novel attention, custom normalization), detailing all 2^3 configurations.
modules.outcome: Design rigorous ablation matrices that withstand peer review scrutiny and scientifically justify every architectural design choice.

modules.name: Baseline Selection: Fair Comparisons, Tuning Baselines & SOTA Claims

objectives.text: - Select state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines, canonical historical baselines, and simple heuristic baselines to establish meaningful performance bounds.
- Avoid the "weak baseline" trap: ensure published baseline implementations are tuned with identical diligence and compute resources as the proposed method.
- Re-run baselines in your own standardized experimental codebase rather than copying numbers from prior papers evaluated under different protocols.
- Define what constitutes a genuine "State of the Art" (SOTA) claim and when to state nuanced findings instead of sweeping superiority claims.
- Report negative results and failure modes where the proposed method underperforms baselines (e.g., high latency, out-of-distribution fragility).
- Document all software versions, hardware configurations, batch sizes, and seeds for both candidate models and reproduced baselines.

modules.mentalModel: Be your own harshest reviewer; tuning the baseline to be as strong as possible makes your final scientific breakthrough indisputable.
modules.tryIt: Re-implement a published baseline on a benchmark dataset, optimize its learning rate and weight decay, and compare against the original paper's reported score.
modules.outcome: Select and tune competitive baselines fairly, avoid misleading comparative claims, and conduct honest state-of-the-art benchmarking.

modules.name: Hyperparameter Optimization Protocols: Random, Grid & Bayesian Search

objectives.text: - Understand why manual trial-and-error hyperparameter tuning introduces researcher bias and invalidates scientific comparisons.
- Implement automated search strategies: grid search for low-dimensional discrete spaces and random search for high-dimensional continuous spaces.
- Leverage Bayesian optimization (Gaussian Processes, Tree-structured Parzen Estimators via Optuna) for compute-efficient exploration.
- Establish equal hyperparameter search budgets (identical trial counts, identical GPU wall-clock hours) for both the proposed model and all baselines.
- Report the full distribution of hyperparameter trial outcomes rather than only the single best cherry-picked run.
- Plot hyperparameter sensitivity curves showing model robustness against variations in learning rate, weight decay, and temperature parameters.

modules.mentalModel: Hyperparameter tuning is an optimization landscape; a method that requires fragile, razor-thin tuning is practically inferior to a robust one.

modules.name: Validation Protocols: Out-of-Distribution Generalization & Leakage Prevention

objectives.text: - Implement stratified k-fold cross-validation and grouped k-fold cross-validation to prevent group-level or user-level data correlation between splits.
- Design out-of-distribution (OOD) test splits evaluating temporal shift (train on past, test on future), domain shift, and geographic shift.

- Enforce strict separation between the development validation split (used for model selection) and the held-out final test split (evaluated once).

modules.mentalModel: The test set is a sacred, sealed envelope opened exactly once at the conclusion of research; peeking inside invalidates your conclusions.
modules.tryIt: Audit a data loading pipeline using automated hash checks to verify that zero sample overlap exists between training, validation, and test splits.
modules.outcome: Design rigorous validation splits, evaluate out-of-distribution robustness, and eliminate all vectors of data leakage.

levels.title: Deep Learning Research Prototyping in PyTorch & JAX
levels.scope: Master the engineering craft of deep learning research prototyping: building modular research codebases, implementing custom autograd operators, mastering numerical precision (BF16/FP16), custom loss surgery, and hardware memory profiling in PyTorch and JAX.

modules.name: Modular Research Codebase Architecture: PyTorch Lightning & Clean JAX

objectives.text: - Decouple research components into clean object-oriented modules: LightningDataModule, LightningModule, and custom Callback hooks.
- Structure model codebases with clear abstraction boundaries between foundational backbone networks, projection heads, and loss functions.
- Eliminate training boilerplate using PyTorch Lightning while preserving low-level control over optimizer steps, gradient clipping, and manual backward passes.
- Understand pure functional programming paradigms in JAX: stateless transformations, explicit pseudo-random key management (jax.random.split), and PRNG keys.

objectives.group: Functional Research Prototyping in JAX & Equinox

modules.outcome: Structure modular, extensible research codebases in both PyTorch and JAX, decoupling modeling logic from infrastructure code.

modules.name: Extending Autograd: Custom Forward-Backward Operators & Matrix Derivatives

objectives.text: - Implement custom PyTorch differentiable operations by subclassing torch.autograd.Function with explicit forward and backward static methods.
- Save necessary intermediate activation tensors using ctx.save_for_backward() while avoiding memory leaks and circular reference references.
- Derive and implement backward vector-Jacobian products (VJPs) for novel custom matrix and tensor operations.
- Verify custom backward gradient implementations against finite-difference approximations using torch.autograd.gradcheck().
- Handle non-differentiable points and subgradient approximations (e.g., custom activations, clamped gradients, straight-through estimators).
- Custom VJPs and custom JVP primitives in JAX using jax.custom_vjp and jax.custom_jvp for custom mathematical primitives.

modules.mentalModel: Autograd functions allow a researcher to introduce non-standard mathematical operators into neural networks while maintaining full end-to-end differentiability.
modules.tryIt: Implement a custom normalized Euclidean distance layer by subclassing torch.autograd.Function, and pass gradcheck with strict tolerance.
modules.outcome: Author custom differentiable operators, derive analytical vector-Jacobian products, and verify numerical gradient accuracy.

modules.name: Numerical Stability, Mixed Precision (BF16/FP16) & Loss Scaling

objectives.text: - Understand IEEE 754 floating-point representations: dynamic range, exponent bits, and mantissa bits in FP32, FP16, and BF16.
- Identify the root causes of numerical instability in research models: catastrophic cancellation, underflow, overflow, and division by zero.
- Implement numerically stable primitives: the log-sum-exp trick for Softmax, epsilon clamps in denominators, and safe cross-entropy losses.
- Implement mixed-precision training in PyTorch using torch.amp.autocast() with BF16 on modern hardware (Ampere, Hopper).
- Apply torch.amp.GradScaler() when using FP16 to dynamically scale small gradient magnitudes and prevent zero-underflow during backward passes.
- Diagnose and debug NaN/Inf generation during training by attaching gradient hooks and using torch.autograd.set_detect_anomaly(True).

modules.mentalModel: BF16 trades precision for dynamic range, matching FP32's exponent bits and eliminating the need for delicate loss scaling.
modules.tryIt: Trigger an intentional numerical underflow in a custom Softmax function, observe NaN loss values, and rewrite it using the stable log-sum-exp formulation.
modules.outcome: Train deep models stably in mixed precision (BF16/FP16), eliminate NaN loss crashes, and master floating-point numerical stability.

modules.name: Custom Loss Formulations, Regularization Penalties & Gradient Surgery

objectives.text: - Implement advanced custom loss objectives: focal loss, contrastive InfoNCE, cosine margin losses, and Wasserstein distance approximations.
- Balance multi-task loss objectives dynamically using learned task weights, homoscedastic uncertainty weighting, or gradient normalization (GradNorm).
- Add custom spectral regularizers (Frobenius norms, nuclear norm penalties, orthogonal weight constraints) directly to loss expressions.
- Implement gradient clipping by norm (torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_) and gradient clipping by value to stabilize deep networks.
- Apply gradient surgery techniques: projected gradient descent, gradient projection to mitigate conflicting task gradients (PCGrad).
- Inspect layer-wise gradient norms during training to diagnose vanishing gradients in early layers or exploding gradients in attention heads.

modules.mentalModel: The loss function is a researcher's steerage mechanism; gradient surgery ensures that competing loss terms do not destructively cancel each other out.
modules.tryIt: Implement the PCGrad algorithm to project conflicting multi-task gradients onto the normal plane of conflicting tasks, verifying improved multi-task stability.
modules.outcome: Formulate novel loss functions, balance multi-objective optimization, and apply gradient surgery to resolve training instabilities.

modules.name: Research Performance Profiling: Memory Snapshots, CUDA Streams & FLOP Counters

objectives.text: - Differentiate between allocated GPU memory, cached reserved memory, and peak memory usage using torch.cuda.memory_allocated() and memory_reserved().
- Capture and inspect interactive HTML memory snapshots using torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history() to pinpoint activation memory spikes.
- Apply activation checkpointing (gradient checkpointing) to trade off recomputation compute for dramatic GPU memory footprint reductions.
- Profile model execution bottlenecks using torch.profiler, identifying CPU-GPU synchronization stalls, kernel launch latencies, and CUDA idle bubbles.
- Count exact floating-point operations (FLOPs) and parameter counts using fvcore, deepspeed.profiling, or torch_tb_profiler.
- Optimize asynchronous CUDA memory transfers by utilizing non-blocking tensor copies, pinned host memory, and dedicated CUDA streams.

modules.mentalModel: Profiling reveals the true hardware cost of your architectural innovation, turning abstract computational complexity into concrete milliseconds and gigabytes.
modules.tryIt: Profile a model with torch.profiler, identify a CPU-bound data loading bottleneck, and resolve it using pinned memory and non-blocking CUDA transfers.
modules.outcome: Profile GPU memory and execution latencies rigorously, eliminate compute bottlenecks, and optimize research code for high throughput.

levels.title: Core Modeling Paradigms: Architectures & Representations
levels.scope: Master foundational modeling paradigms and representation learning from first principles: the Transformer architecture, attention variants, rotary embeddings (RoPE), State Space Models (Mamba), self-supervised representation objectives, and geometric deep learning.

modules.name: The Transformer Blueprint: Attention Mechanics, KV Cache & Scaled Dot Products

objectives.text: - Derive scaled dot-product attention from first principles: query-key compatibility, square-root dimension scaling, and Softmax normalization.
- Implement multi-head self-attention and cross-attention from scratch, managing tensor projections, head splitting, and output transformations.
- Analyze the quadratic time and memory complexity O(N^2) of standard attention with respect to sequence length N.
- Understand autoregressive sequence generation dynamics and the computational redundancy of re-computing past key and value vectors.
- Implement a key-value (KV) cache for fast autoregressive decoding, managing rolling tensor buffers across generation timesteps.
- Implement modern attention memory optimizations: Multi-Query Attention (MQA) and Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) to reduce KV cache memory footprints.

modules.mentalModel: Multi-head attention is a soft, content-addressable memory retrieval mechanism; the KV cache prevents redundant historical recomputation.
modules.tryIt: Implement a self-attention module from scratch in PyTorch with Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) and verify output tensor shapes and parity against torch.nn.MultiheadAttention.
modules.outcome: Build, modify, and optimize multi-head attention mechanisms from mathematical equations, including low-overhead KV caching.

modules.name: Advanced Context & Positional Inductive Biases: RoPE, ALiBi & Linear Attention

objectives.text: - Understand why absolute sinusoidal position embeddings fail to generalize to sequence lengths beyond the training horizon.
- Derive Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) mathematically as complex number rotations of 2D coordinate pairs in query and key feature spaces.
- Implement RoPE from scratch in PyTorch, applying 2D complex rotations and inspecting the decay of inner products with increasing relative distance.
- Implement Attention with Linear Biases (ALiBi), penalizing query-key attention scores with static linear distance biases for zero-shot length extrapolation.
- Analyze linear attention approximations (Kernelized Attention, Performer, Linear Transformer) and their computational trade-offs.
- Understand the hardware-aware design of FlashAttention: GPU SRAM tiling, online Softmax computation, and avoiding HBM read/write roundtrips.

modules.mentalModel: RoPE injects relative positional information purely through geometric rotations of the query and key vectors without altering their magnitudes.
modules.tryIt: Implement RoPE vector rotations on a toy sequence, and compute the attention matrix to visualize the natural decay of attention weights over distance.
modules.outcome: Implement modern positional encoding schemes (RoPE, ALiBi) and analyze long-context extrapolation mechanisms in foundation models.

modules.name: Sub-Quadratic State Space Models: S4, Mamba & Hybrid Sequence Architectures

objectives.text: - Formulate linear time-invariant (LTI) continuous state space models dx/dt = Ax + Bu, y = Cx + Du from classical control theory.
- Discretize continuous state space equations into discrete recurrence relations using the bilinear (Tustin) or zero-order hold (ZOH) transformation.
- Master the Structured State Space (S4) model: HiPPO matrix initialization for long-range memory and dual computation (recurrent inference, convolutional training).
- Understand the limitation of LTI state space models: static, input-independent transition matrices that cannot perform selective in-context filtering.

objectives.text: - Implement the selective scan mechanism of Mamba where B, C, and delta matrices become dynamic, input-dependent functions of token embeddings.
objectives.group: Selective State Spaces & The Mamba Architecture

objectives.text: - Analyze the linear O(N) sequence length complexity of Mamba and evaluate hybrid Transformer-SSM architectural designs.
objectives.group: Selective State Spaces & The Mamba Architecture

modules.mentalModel: Transformers are associative memories that re-attend to all history; State Space Models compress history into a continuous latent state vector.
modules.tryIt: Implement a minimal selective state space scan function in PyTorch, compare its linear scaling against quadratic attention on 16k sequence lengths.
modules.outcome: Master modern sub-quadratic sequence models (S4, Mamba), understand state space discretization, and evaluate hybrid architectures.

modules.name: Self-Supervised Learning: Contrastive InfoNCE, SimCLR & Masked Autoencoding

objectives.text: - Understand the manifold hypothesis: high-dimensional real-world data concentrates along lower-dimensional continuous geometric sub-manifolds.
- Derive the InfoNCE contrastive loss function from lower bounds on mutual information between augmented views.
- Implement contrastive learning architectures (SimCLR, MoCo) with positive pair generation, negative queue caching, and temperature scaling.
- Analyze collapse modes in representation learning (dimensional collapse, complete representation collapse) and how stop-gradient methods prevent them (BYOL, SimSiam).
- Implement redundancy reduction methods (Barlow Twins) by driving the cross-correlation matrix of dual representations toward the identity matrix.
- Master Masked Autoencoders (MAE): high-ratio token masking, asymmetric encoder-decoder architectures, and pixel-level reconstruction objectives.

modules.mentalModel: Contrastive learning pulls augmented views of the same instance together while pushing distinct instances apart across a hyperspherical latent space.
modules.tryIt: Train a small representation encoder using InfoNCE loss on unlabelled image patches, and evaluate representation quality via linear probe accuracy.
modules.outcome: Formulate self-supervised learning objectives, prevent representation collapse, and train rich latent encoders without human labels.

modules.name: Geometric Deep Learning: Graph Neural Networks & Equivariant Representations

objectives.text: - Represent relational scientific data (molecules, knowledge graphs, citation networks) as graph structures with node, edge, and global feature tensors.
- Derive the general Message Passing Neural Network (MPNN) paradigm: message computation, neighborhood aggregation, and node state updates.
- Implement Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) and Graph Attention Networks (GAT) with dynamic edge attention coefficients.
- Formalize permutation invariance and permutation equivariance in deep learning architectures over graph and point-cloud structures.
- Understand geometric symmetry groups: Euclidean group E(3), special Euclidean group SE(3), and rotation group SO(3) in scientific modeling.
- Master E(n)-equivariant neural networks (EGNN) and their applications in modeling molecular conformations and 3D molecular structures.

modules.mentalModel: Deep learning succeeds by encoding the physical symmetries of the problem domain as structural inductive biases in the network architecture.
modules.tryIt: Implement an MPNN message passing layer from scratch in PyTorch, verifying that node permutations produce identical permuted output representations.
modules.outcome: Build Graph Neural Networks from first principles, understand geometric equivariance, and apply symmetry constraints to scientific data.

levels.title: Generative Modeling & Probabilistic Machine Learning
levels.scope: Master the mathematical formulations and empirical execution of modern generative modeling: Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), continuous-time score-based diffusion models (DDPM, SDEs), Flow Matching on probability manifolds, and rigorous distribution evaluation metrics.

modules.name: Variational Inference, Latent Variable Models & The ELBO Objective

objectives.text: - Formulate directed latent variable models p(x) = \int p(x|z) p(z) dz and understand the intractability of the true marginal likelihood and posterior.
- Introduce the variational distribution q_phi(z|x) and derive the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) mathematically using Jensen's inequality and KL divergence.
- Deconstruct the ELBO into the reconstruction likelihood term and the latent prior regularization term.
- Analyze why the naive gradient estimator has high variance and derive the reparameterization trick z = mu + sigma * epsilon for backpropagation.
- Implement the standard Variational Autoencoder (VAE) from scratch in PyTorch with Gaussian encoder and decoder networks.
- Address posterior collapse in VAEs using KL annealing schedules, free bits, and vector quantization (VQ-VAE with straight-through estimators).

modules.mentalModel: The ELBO trades off accurate reconstruction of empirical data against keeping the latent distribution close to a tractable Gaussian prior.
modules.tryIt: Implement a VAE on image data, apply the reparameterization trick, and inspect the latent space by generating samples along a 2D latent grid traversal.
modules.outcome: Derive and implement Variational Autoencoders from first principles and resolve posterior collapse in deep latent variable models.

modules.name: Score-Based Generative Modeling & Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM)

objectives.text: - Define the forward Markovian noising chain q(x_t | x_{t-1}) corrupting data into isotropic Gaussian noise according to variance schedule beta_t.
- Derive the closed-form transition distribution q(x_t | x_0) = N(x_t; sqrt(alpha_bar_t) x_0, (1 - alpha_bar_t) I) for arbitrary timestep t.
- Implement the forward noising loop in PyTorch, generating noisy tensors at arbitrary timesteps without recursive iteration.
- Formulate the reverse denoising process p_theta(x_{t-1} | x_t) parameterized by a deep neural network (U-Net or Diffusion Transformer DiT).
objectives.group: The Reverse Denoising Process & The Simplified Loss

objectives.text: - Derive the variational bound on negative log-likelihood for diffusion models and reduce it to the simplified epsilon-prediction objective L_simple.
objectives.group: The Reverse Denoising Process & The Simplified Loss

objectives.text: - Implement the DDPM training loop, sampling random timesteps, injecting Gaussian noise, and computing the MSE loss between true and predicted noise.
objectives.group: The Reverse Denoising Process & The Simplified Loss

modules.mentalModel: Forward diffusion systematically destroys information; reverse diffusion trains a neural network to invert thermodynamic entropy.
modules.tryIt: Implement the forward noising formula in PyTorch, verify that clean samples degenerate into isotropic Gaussian noise at t=1000, and write the training loss.
modules.outcome: Derive the forward and reverse DDPM equations analytically and implement end-to-end diffusion training loops.

modules.name: Continuous-Time Diffusion: Itô Stochastic Differential Equations & ODE Sampling

objectives.text: - Generalize discrete diffusion timesteps into continuous-time Itô Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs): dx = f(x, t) dt + g(t) dw.
- Classify variance preserving (VP), variance exploding (VE), and sub-VP continuous diffusion processes.
- Formulate the Anderson reverse-time SDE theorem, showing that reversing an SDE requires estimating the score function \nabla_x log p_t(x).
- Derive the deterministic Probability Flow ODE that shares identical marginal probability densities p_t(x) with the continuous SDE.
- Leverage numerical ODE solvers (Euler, Runge-Kutta, DPM-Solver) to achieve high-quality generation in 10-25 steps instead of 1,000 steps.
- Implement Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG): training conditionally with randomly dropped labels and extrapolating along the conditional score vector.

modules.mentalModel: The Probability Flow ODE defines a deterministic vector field that smoothly maps random Gaussian noise into the data distribution manifold.
modules.tryIt: Implement a predictor-corrector sampler and an accelerated ODE solver in PyTorch, comparing sample generation quality and step counts.
modules.outcome: Master continuous-time SDE/ODE diffusion formulations, implement Classifier-Free Guidance, and accelerate reverse sampling.

modules.name: Flow Matching & Optimal Transport on Probability Manifolds

objectives.text: - Formulate Continuous Normalizing Flows (CNFs) where a time-dependent vector field v_t(x) generates a continuous probability path from p_0 to p_1.
- Understand the intractability of standard CNF maximum likelihood training and introduce the Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) objective (Lipman et al.).
- Derive the regression loss ||v_theta(x_t, t) - u_t(x | x_1)||^2, proving that marginal vector fields can be learned via conditional flow targets.
- Compare standard Brownian diffusion paths with Optimal Transport (OT) displacement paths: straight lines connecting noise p_0 to data p_1.
- Implement Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching (OT-CFM): linear trajectories x_t = (1 - t) x_0 + t x_1 with constant velocity v_t = x_1 - x_0.
- Analyze the advantages of straight flow trajectories: faster numerical integration, lower curvature, and exceptional sample quality in few steps.

modules.mentalModel: Diffusion takes a stochastic random walk through noise; Optimal Transport Flow Matching travels along straight, minimal-energy geodesic lines.
modules.tryIt: Train a 2D toy Flow Matching model to transform a Gaussian distribution into a two-moons distribution using straight-line OT trajectories.
modules.outcome: Derive the Conditional Flow Matching objective, implement Optimal Transport probability paths, and train vector field models.

modules.name: Empirical Evaluation of Generative Distributions: FID, Precision, Recall & Density

objectives.text: - Understand the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) metric: extracting deep feature representations and computing the Wasserstein-2 distance between Gaussians.
- Implement the analytical Fréchet distance formula: ||mu_1 - mu_2||^2 + Tr(Sigma_1 + Sigma_2 - 2 (Sigma_1 Sigma_2)^{1/2}).
- Identify FID failure modes: sensitivity to sample count (bias at low N), image resolution, JPEG compression artifacts, and feature extractor biases.
- Disentangle generative sample fidelity from distribution coverage using Precision and Recall metrics for generative models (Sajjadi et al.).
objectives.group: Disentangling Quality vs Diversity: Precision, Recall, Coverage & Density

objectives.text: - Implement Density and Coverage metrics to detect mode dropping, mode collapse, and out-of-distribution hallucinations.
objectives.group: Disentangling Quality vs Diversity: Precision, Recall, Coverage & Density

objectives.text: - Evaluate perceptual metrics (LPIPS, CLIP-Score) and compute distribution distance across scientific feature spaces.
objectives.group: Disentangling Quality vs Diversity: Precision, Recall, Coverage & Density

modules.mentalModel: FID provides a single composite distance score; precision measures how realistic samples are, while recall measures how many modes were covered.
modules.tryIt: Compute the exact FID between a generated sample set and a validation set using clean-fid, verifying sensitivity to sample size and image resizing.
modules.outcome: Evaluate generative models with statistical rigor, compute FID/IS accurately, and diagnose mode collapse using precision-recall metrics.

levels.title: Reinforcement Learning, Search & Test-Time Reasoning
levels.scope: Master reinforcement learning, planning, and test-time reasoning in AI research: Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), policy optimization (PPO, SAC), search algorithms (MCTS, Tree-of-Thoughts), Process Reward Models (PRMs), and test-time compute scaling laws.

modules.name: Markov Decision Processes, Dynamic Programming & Bellman Optimality

objectives.text: - Formulate the reinforcement learning problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP): state space S, action space A, transition probability P, reward function R, and discount factor gamma.
- Formalize policies pi(a|s), state-value functions V^pi(s), and action-value functions Q^pi(s, a) under infinite-horizon discounted return objectives.
- Derive the Bellman Expectation Equations for V^pi and Q^pi by unrolling the recursive definition of expected discounted return.
- State and prove the Bellman Contraction Mapping theorem under the L-infinity norm, establishing the existence and uniqueness of the optimal value function Q*.
- Implement exact dynamic programming algorithms: Policy Iteration (alternating policy evaluation and policy improvement) and Value Iteration.
- Analyze the curse of dimensionality in continuous state and action spaces, motivating deep parametric function approximation.

modules.mentalModel: The Bellman equation is a recursive consistency constraint; dynamic programming contracts arbitrary value guesses toward the true optimal policy.
modules.tryIt: Implement Value Iteration in Python for a discrete gridworld MDP, verify contraction mapping convergence rates, and extract the optimal deterministic policy.
modules.outcome: Formulate sequential decision-making problems as MDPs and derive the fundamental convergence proofs of dynamic programming.

modules.name: Deep Q-Networks & Value Function Approximation Stability

objectives.text: - Approximate action-value functions using deep neural networks Q_theta(s, a) and formulate the temporal difference (TD) loss objective.
- Identify the root causes of instability in non-linear value approximation: non-stationary target distributions, correlated data streams, and policy oscillations.
- Implement the core Deep Q-Network (DQN) stabilizing mechanisms: experience replay buffer sampling and decoupled frozen target networks Q_target.
- Mitigate overestimation bias in action-value updates using Double DQN (DDQN), decoupling action selection from value evaluation.
- Implement Dueling DQN architectures, decomposing Q(s, a) into independent state value V(s) and state-dependent action advantage A(s, a) streams.
- Master Prioritized Experience Replay (PER), sampling historical transitions according to TD-error magnitudes with importance-sampling correction weights.

modules.mentalModel: Double DQN prevents maximization bias: the main network nominates the best action, while the target network calculates its honest value.
modules.tryIt: Implement a Deep Q-Network from scratch in PyTorch with experience replay and target networks, training it to solve the CartPole-v1 benchmark environment.
modules.outcome: Build stable deep Q-learning architectures and eliminate maximization bias using Double DQN and dueling streams.

modules.name: Policy Gradients, Trust Region Policy Optimization (TRPO) & PPO

objectives.text: - Derive the Policy Gradient Theorem analytically: \nabla_theta J(theta) = E_{tau ~ pi_theta}[\sum_t \nabla_theta log pi_theta(a_t|s_t) G_t].
- Implement the REINFORCE algorithm with baseline subtraction to reduce gradient variance without introducing estimator bias.
- Formulate Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE), balancing the bias-variance trade-off in temporal difference returns using the exponential decay factor lambda.
- Understand policy collapse: small parameter updates in neural policies can cause catastrophic performance degradation from which the agent cannot recover.
objectives.group: Trust Region Methods & Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)

objectives.text: - Formulate the Trust Region Policy Optimization (TRPO) objective enforcing a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence constraint D_KL(pi_old || pi) <= delta.
objectives.group: Trust Region Methods & Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)

objectives.text: - Implement Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO): the clipped surrogate objective L_CLIP(theta) bounding policy probability ratios without expensive second-order Hessian computation.
objectives.group: Trust Region Methods & Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)

modules.mentalModel: PPO's clipped objective is an insurance policy: it forbids the policy from changing too dramatically in a single update step.
modules.tryIt: Implement the PPO clipped objective function in PyTorch, verify that gradient updates are zeroed out when probability ratios exceed 1 + epsilon or 1 - epsilon.
modules.outcome: Derive the policy gradient theorem, implement Generalized Advantage Estimation, and master Proximal Policy Optimization.

modules.name: Test-Time Reasoning: Chain-of-Thought, Tree-of-Thoughts & MCTS Search

objectives.text: - Analyze the computational expressivity of autoregressive Transformers: constant-depth circuit limitations on complex multi-step reasoning tasks.
- Formalize Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting as allocating additional dynamic runtime token steps, increasing effective computational circuit depth.
- Differentiate between zero-shot CoT ("Let's think step by step"), few-shot exemplar demonstrations, and self-consistency voting across multiple sampled traces.
- Formulate reasoning as explicit search over a state space of intermediate thoughts: the Tree of Thoughts (ToT) framework.
objectives.group: Structured Search Over Latent Thought Spaces

objectives.text: - Implement graph search heuristics over thought trees: breadth-first search (BFS), depth-first search (DFS) with backtracking, and beam search.
objectives.group: Structured Search Over Latent Thought Spaces

objectives.text: - Master Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) for language model reasoning: Selection (PUCT formula), Expansion, Rollout/Evaluation, and Backpropagation.
objectives.group: Structured Search Over Latent Thought Spaces

modules.mentalModel: Autoregressive decoding is a single greedy walk through thought space; MCTS explores a branching tree of alternative deduction paths.
modules.tryIt: Implement a Tree of Thoughts search controller in Python using an LLM API, solving a complex mathematical puzzle via systematic branching and pruning.
modules.outcome: Formalize test-time reasoning as computational search, implement Tree-of-Thoughts, and integrate Monte Carlo Tree Search.

modules.name: Process vs. Outcome Supervision: Training Process Reward Models (PRMs)

objectives.text: - Analyze Outcome Reward Models (ORMs): assigning a single binary scalar reward at the conclusion of a multi-step reasoning trajectory.
objectives.group: The Limits of Outcome Reward Models (ORMs)

objectives.text: - Identify the credit assignment problem in ORMs: intermediate logical errors receive positive credit if the final answer is accidentally correct (false positives).
objectives.group: The Limits of Outcome Reward Models (ORMs)

objectives.text: - Understand step-level reward hacking where models generate degenerate or repetitive intermediate derivations to satisfy coarse outcome signals.
objectives.group: The Limits of Outcome Reward Models (ORMs)

objectives.text: - Formulate Process Reward Models (PRMs): predicting the step-by-step correctness probability r_t \in [0, 1] for every individual deduction step.
- Implement step-level synthetic data collection protocols: automated verification rollouts, Monte Carlo value estimation, and active learning annotation.
- Evaluate search efficiency: compare Best-of-N selection and guided beam search steered by PRMs versus standard ORMs on mathematical reasoning benchmarks (MATH, GSM8K).

modules.mentalModel: An ORM only checks the final destination; a PRM acts as an experienced mathematician grading every individual step on the chalkboard.
modules.tryIt: Train a step-level verification classifier on mathematical solutions, score multi-step traces, and use PRM scores to guide a beam search decoder.
modules.outcome: Implement Process Reward Models from scratch, solve credit assignment in multi-step reasoning, and steer test-time search.

levels.title: Benchmark Creation, Data Curation & Evaluation Science
levels.scope: Master the scientific discipline of dataset curation, benchmark construction, and evaluation rigor: construct validity, annotation agreement statistics (Kappa, Alpha), contamination detection, LLM-as-a-judge calibration, and adversarial robustness testing.

modules.name: Designing Novel Academic Benchmarks: Construct Validity & Hardness Curves

objectives.text: - Understand construct validity: ensuring that a benchmark quantitatively measures the intended cognitive or computational capability rather than superficial surface correlations.
- Avoid common benchmark failure modes: shortcut learning, dataset artifact exploitation, and uncalibrated multiple-choice guessing.
- Structure multi-task benchmark suites across distinct difficulty tiers (easy, intermediate, frontier) with clear task stratification.
- Measure the discriminative power of individual benchmark evaluation items using Item Response Theory (IRT) and difficulty curves.
- Detect ceiling effects (where SOTA models saturate performance) and floor effects (where all models perform at random chance).
- Design dynamic, living benchmarks that continuously evolve to prevent model overfitting to static benchmark distributions over time.

modules.mentalModel: A benchmark is a scientific instrument; if the instrument is calibrated on spurious artifacts, all subsequent scientific discoveries are illusions.
modules.tryIt: Analyze a popular benchmark dataset, identify five examples where a model could predict the correct label using spurious surface heuristics, and fix them.
modules.outcome: Author novel, robust academic benchmarks with verified construct validity and calibrated discriminative hardness curves.

modules.name: Data Curation Protocols: Deduplication, Quality Classifiers & Synthetic Generation

objectives.text: - Implement large-scale text preprocessing pipelines: language identification, rule-based heuristic filtering, and toxic content masking.
- Train high-precision domain quality classifiers (fastText, shallow Transformer classifiers) to filter noisy web crawls into textbook-quality corpora.
- Master scalable document deduplication: MinHash locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) and exact substring deduplication to prevent memorization.
- Design synthetic data generation workflows using frontier LLMs: prompt inversion, seed task expansion, and tree-structured problem generation.
objectives.group: Synthetic Data Generation & Data Contamination Risk

objectives.text: - Implement automated verification and filtering pipelines: discard hallucinated synthetic reasoning traces using symbolic verifiers and Python sandboxes.
objectives.group: Synthetic Data Generation & Data Contamination Risk

objectives.text: - Monitor model collapse dynamics: quantify the degradation in linguistic diversity and tail-distribution collapse when models train recursively on synthetic data.
objectives.group: Synthetic Data Generation & Data Contamination Risk

modules.mentalModel: High-quality data is the primary driver of capability; filtering out 80% of low-quality tokens yields superior models with lower compute.
modules.tryIt: Build a data curation pipeline implementing MinHash LSH deduplication and a fastText quality classifier, filtering a raw dataset into a clean research corpus.
modules.outcome: Curate high-quality scientific datasets, execute massive-scale deduplication, and generate robust synthetic data with automated verification.

modules.name: Human Annotation Science: Inter-Annotator Agreement (Kappa, Alpha) & Quality Control

objectives.text: - Author exhaustive, unambiguous annotation codebooks specifying label definitions, positive examples, edge cases, and tie-breaking rules.
- Compute pairwise inter-annotator agreement metrics: Cohen’s kappa for two raters and Fleiss’ kappa for multiple fixed raters.
- Apply Krippendorff’s alpha for flexible reliability estimation across arbitrary numbers of raters, missing data, and non-nominal scale types.
- Implement qualification screening tests, attention-check honey-pot instances, and rater velocity monitoring to detect low-effort crowd workers.
- Differentiate between genuine task ambiguity (high epistemic uncertainty) versus low rater competence when resolving annotation disagreements.
- Aggregate multi-annotator distributions using Dawid-Skene latent truth modeling rather than naive majority voting.

modules.mentalModel: Inter-annotator agreement quantifies the objective reality of your task; if expert humans cannot agree (alpha < 0.67), a machine cannot learn it.
modules.tryIt: Conduct an annotation pilot with three raters on 100 complex domain examples, calculate Krippendorff's alpha, and revise the guidelines to resolve ambiguities.
modules.outcome: Design rigorous human annotation protocols, compute statistical agreement metrics, and resolve labeling disagreements with latent truth models.

modules.name: Benchmark Contamination Auditing: Suffix Arrays, n-gram Overlap & Decontamination

objectives.text: - Understand how test-set contamination occurs when benchmark questions, test splits, or solutions leak into web-scale pre-training or fine-tuning corpora.
- Distinguish between verbatim contamination (exact character overlap) versus paraphrased or synthetic contamination.
- Analyze the catastrophic impact of contamination on scientific progress: inflated benchmark scores, false capabilities, and invalid scaling claims.
- Implement scalable n-gram contamination detection algorithms (e.g., 13-gram exact match scanning) across massive multi-terabyte corpora.
- Build suffix arrays and inverted indices to identify verbatim substring overlaps between evaluation test sets and training token sets.
- Execute automated decontamination protocols: remove contaminated documents or generate clean, private benchmark test splits with verified zero overlap.

modules.mentalModel: Benchmark contamination is the AI equivalent of leaking the final exam before the semester starts; clean science requires strict quarantine.
modules.tryIt: Build a 13-gram contamination scanner using a suffix array, index a training corpus, and measure the exact contamination rate against a benchmark test set.
modules.outcome: Audit research corpora for benchmark contamination, build scalable n-gram detectors, and guarantee pristine evaluation splits.

modules.name: LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation: Calibrating Biases, Win-Rates & Bradley-Terry Elo

objectives.text: - Understand the methodology of using frontier models as automated evaluators (LLM-as-a-Judge) for open-ended generation, reasoning, and alignment.
- Implement structured pairwise comparison and single-answer scoring prompts with detailed rubrics and chain-of-thought justification.
- Quantify human-to-LLM judge correlation (Spearman rank correlation, Kendall’s tau) to validate judge reliability against human ground truth.
- Identify systematic failure modes in LLM judges: position bias (favoring candidate A), verbosity bias (favoring longer responses), and self-enhancement bias.
- Implement mitigation protocols: bidirectional evaluation (averaging swapped A/B orderings), length-normalized scoring, and multi-model judge ensembles.
- Compute global competitive rankings using the Bradley-Terry probabilistic model and maximum likelihood Elo rating systems (LMSYS Chatbot Arena methodology).

modules.mentalModel: An LLM judge is a biased human surrogate; swapping candidate order and controlling for token length prevents superficial vanity scoring.
modules.tryIt: Implement a pairwise LLM evaluation script with bidirectional order swapping, compute candidate win-rates, and estimate Bradley-Terry Elo ratings.
modules.outcome: Deploy calibrated LLM-as-a-judge pipelines, eliminate position and verbosity biases, and calculate robust Bradley-Terry Elo rankings.

levels.title: High-Performance Computing (HPC) & Scaled Research Systems
levels.scope: Master the computational infrastructure of modern large-scale machine learning research: operating on HPC supercomputing clusters with SLURM, distributed communication primitives (NCCL), multi-GPU training (DDP, FSDP), 3D parallelism (Megatron-LM, ZeRO-3), and measuring Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU).
