modules.name: Supercomputing Cluster Architecture: SLURM Schedulers, Modules & InfiniBand Fabrics

objectives.text: - Understand high-performance computing (HPC) cluster topologies: login nodes, compute nodes, shared Lustre/GPFS parallel filesystems, and scratch storage.
- Manage cluster resource allocation using the SLURM workload manager: sbatch scripts, srun interactive allocations, squeue monitoring, and scancel.
- Configure SLURM job submission parameters: GPU counts (--gpus-per-node), CPU cores, memory limits, job arrays, and dependency chains.
- Load and configure environment modules (Lmod) to access specific CUDA toolkits, cuDNN libraries, OpenMPI distributions, and compiler toolchains.
- Understand high-speed cluster networking fabrics: InfiniBand (HDR, NDR), RoCE, Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA), and PCIe Gen4/Gen5 lane topology.
- Measure inter-node and intra-node network latency and bandwidth using nccl-tests and InfiniBand diagnostics (ibv_devinfo, ib_write_bw).

modules.mentalModel: A supercomputer is not just many servers; it is a single, tightly coupled distributed instrument synchronized across a low-latency network fabric.
modules.tryIt: Write a multi-GPU SLURM batch submission script requesting 4 GPUs on a single node, redirecting stdout/stderr, and verifying environment module initialization.
modules.outcome: Operate on university and national supercomputing clusters using SLURM, manage HPC modules, and diagnose interconnect topologies.

modules.name: Collective Communication Primitives: Ring All-Reduce, NCCL & Hardware Topologies

objectives.text: - Formalize distributed collective communication operations: Broadcast, Scatter, Gather, All-Gather, Reduce, Reduce-Scatter, and All-Reduce.
- Derive the communication volume and time complexity of the Ring All-Reduce algorithm across N participating compute ranks.
- Prove that Ring All-Reduce transfers exactly 2 * ((N - 1) / N) * S bytes per GPU, making communication bandwidth independent of cluster size N.
- Understand the role of NCCL as the high-performance communication backbone for multi-GPU PyTorch training.
- Configure NCCL ring and tree communication topologies across NVLink bridges within nodes and InfiniBand adapters between nodes.
- Debug distributed communication stalls and deadlocks using NCCL debug environment variables (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL).

modules.mentalModel: Ring All-Reduce splits gradient tensors into chunks that flow in a circle; every GPU sends and receives simultaneously without a master bottleneck.
modules.tryIt: Run an nccl-tests all_reduce_perf benchmark across multiple GPUs, measure effective bus bandwidth (GB/s), and verify near-theoretical saturation.
modules.outcome: Derive collective communication algorithms analytically, configure NCCL parameters, and diagnose distributed communication bottlenecks.

modules.name: Distributed Data Parallel (DDP) & Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP)

objectives.text: - Master the execution mechanics of torch.nn.parallel.DistributedDataParallel (DDP): process forking, rank assignments, and local rank mapping.
- Understand gradient bucketing and overlapping: how DDP initiates asynchronous Ring All-Reduce operations while earlier layers are still computing gradients.
- Implement robust distributed initialization with torch.distributed.init_process_group() using the NCCL backend and DistributedSampler.
- Analyze the memory wall of standard DDP: redundant replication of model weights, optimizer states, and gradients across every GPU rank.
- Implement Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP): sharding model parameters, gradients, and optimizer states across ranks, reconstructing weights on the fly.
- Configure FSDP sharding strategies (FULL_SHARD, SHARD_GRAD_OP, NO_SHARD), CPU offloading, and mixed-precision communication policies.

modules.mentalModel: DDP replicates the model everywhere and syncs gradients; FSDP shreds the model across GPUs and gathers layers just in time for execution.
modules.tryIt: Convert a standard PyTorch training loop into a multi-GPU FSDP script, and train a model whose parameter count exceeds single-GPU VRAM capacity.
modules.outcome: Deploy multi-GPU training with PyTorch DDP and FSDP, overlapping compute with communication and breaking single-GPU memory barriers.

modules.name: 3D Parallelism: Tensor Parallelism, Pipeline Parallelism & ZeRO-1/2/3 Memory Sharding

objectives.text: - Deconstruct the exact memory consumption of AdamW optimizer states (16 bytes per parameter in mixed precision).
- Differentiate the three stages of ZeRO: ZeRO-1 (shards optimizer states), ZeRO-2 (shards optimizer states + gradients), and ZeRO-3 (shards everything).
- Implement ZeRO memory reduction using DeepSpeed or native PyTorch FSDP, calculating exact per-GPU memory footprints across cluster sizes.
- Master Megatron-LM Tensor Parallelism: column-parallel linear projections for Q, K, V and row-parallel projections for output matrices.
- Master Pipeline Parallelism: partitioning model layers sequentially across GPU stages with micro-batching to minimize pipeline bubbles (1F1B schedule).
- Understand 3D Parallelism combinations: uniting Data Parallelism (DP), Tensor Parallelism (TP), and Pipeline Parallelism (PP) for frontier model scales.

modules.mentalModel: Tensor Parallelism splits individual matrices across fast NVLink; Pipeline Parallelism splits layers across nodes; Data Parallelism scales across clusters.
modules.tryIt: Calculate the theoretical memory footprint of a 20B parameter model under ZeRO-1, ZeRO-2, and ZeRO-3 across an 8-GPU node.
modules.outcome: Architect large-scale 3D distributed training configurations combining Tensor, Pipeline, and Sharded Data Parallelism.

modules.name: Compute Efficiency Metrics: Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) & Hardware Profiling

objectives.text: - Compute theoretical minimum FLOPs required for forward and backward passes of a Transformer: 6 * N * D (where N is parameters, D is tokens).
- Define Hardware FLOPs Utilization (HFU): the percentage of raw hardware peak floating-point capacity achieved by the cluster during execution.
- Define Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU, Chowdhery et al.): the ratio of theoretical model FLOPs to peak hardware capacity, penalizing recomputation overhead.
- Instrument distributed training runs to calculate and log real-time MFU, achieving target research efficiency benchmarks (MFU > 45-55%).
- Identify causes of low MFU: communication bubbles, activation recomputation overhead, CPU data loading starvation, and memory bandwidth throttling.
- Monitor power consumption, thermal throttling, and calculate the carbon footprint (CO2 equivalent) of large-scale scientific training experiments.

modules.mentalModel: MFU is the supreme benchmark of research systems engineering: it tells you what percentage of your expensive compute budget was genuinely useful math.
modules.tryIt: Write an MFU tracking callback that calculates floating-point throughput at every step, and measure the exact MFU of a distributed training run.
modules.outcome: Compute MFU and HFU rigorously, profile distributed cluster efficiency, and optimize GPU utilization to maximize scientific output per dollar.

levels.title: Pre-Training Dynamics, Scaling Laws & Empirical Science
levels.scope: Master the empirical science of foundation model pre-training: deriving and fitting scaling laws (Kaplan vs. Chinchilla), diagnosing pre-training loss dynamics and loss spikes, data mixture optimization, the scientific debate surrounding emergent abilities, and tokenizer information theory.

modules.name: Empirical Scaling Laws: Kaplan vs. Chinchilla Power-Law Fitting Methodologies

objectives.text: - Formulate the empirical scaling hypothesis: cross-entropy loss scales as a smooth power-law function of compute budget C, dataset size D, and parameter count N.
- Analyze the OpenAI scaling laws (Kaplan et al., 2020): L(N) = (N_c / N)^{alpha_N}, predicting that allocating compute primarily to model size N is optimal.
- Understand the methodology of fitting power laws: running series of small compute-budget models and extrapolating performance across orders of magnitude.
- Deconstruct the DeepMind Chinchilla scaling laws (Hoffmann et al., 2022): L(N, D) = E + A / N^alpha + B / D^beta under compute constraint C \approx 6 * N * D.
- Derive the compute-optimal scaling frontier using the method of Lagrange multipliers, proving that parameters N and tokens D should scale equally (alpha \approx beta \approx 0.5).
- Analyze inference-optimal over-training: why open-source foundation models (Llama, Mistral) train on 15T+ tokens far past the Chinchilla compute-optimal point.

modules.mentalModel: Scaling laws turn speculative pre-training into predictable engineering; fitting curves on 10M models predicts the exact loss of a 70B model.
modules.tryIt: Implement a non-linear least squares optimization function in SciPy, fitting the Chinchilla parametric loss equation to a synthetic matrix of (N, D, Loss) runs.
modules.outcome: Derive and fit empirical scaling laws, calculate compute-optimal parameter allocations, and extrapolate performance across compute budgets.

modules.name: Pre-Training Optimization Dynamics: Loss Spikes, QK-Norm & z-loss Mitigations

objectives.text: - Analyze normal pre-training loss trajectories: rapid initial power-law descent, steady power-law decay, and asymptotic learning saturation.
- Understand optimization schedules: cosine decay schedules, warmup duration, linear decay, and constant learning rate with cooldown phases (MiniCPM, WSD schedule).
- Monitor gradient norms, weight norm growth, and learning rate dynamics across hundreds of thousands of pre-training optimizer steps.
- Identify the root physical causes of catastrophic loss spikes during pre-training: attention logit growth causing extreme Softmax values and gradient explosions.
- Implement Query-Key Normalization (QK-Norm): applying LayerNorm or RMSNorm directly to Q and K tensors before computing scaled dot products.
- Master auxiliary stabilizing loss terms: the z-loss penalty (log^2 \sum e^{z_i}) that explicitly penalizes large unnormalized logits in the output vocabulary head.

modules.mentalModel: A loss spike is a numerical tsunami in the attention layers; QK-Norm acts as a breakwater, bounding logit amplitudes regardless of scale.
modules.tryIt: Simulate an unstable pre-training run with exploding attention logits, observe the loss spike, apply QK-Norm, and verify smooth, spike-free convergence.
modules.outcome: Diagnose pre-training optimization instabilities, eliminate catastrophic loss spikes using QK-Norm, and deploy robust learning rate schedules.

modules.name: Data Mixture Science: Domain Weighting, Synthetic Data Annealing & Curriculum Learning

objectives.text: - Analyze the composition of web-scale pre-training mixtures: web text (Common Crawl), code (GitHub), academic papers (arXiv), and structured knowledge (Wikipedia).
- Conduct data mixture ablation studies: evaluate downstream reasoning, coding, and factual recall as a function of domain mixture percentages.
- Implement automated data weighting: compute gradient alignment between candidate data domains and target evaluation benchmarks (DoReMi methodology).
- Implement curriculum learning in pre-training: transitioning from broad web scrapes to high-quality textbooks, code, and synthetic reasoning datasets.
- Master learning rate cooldown and data annealing: injecting specialized high-quality math and code tokens during the final 10-20% of the training run.
- Evaluate the impact of data freshness, deduplication thresholds, and quality filtering on downstream pre-training sample efficiency.

modules.mentalModel: Model weights are an empirical compression of the data mixture; changing the mixture percentage reshapes the model's fundamental cognitive abilities.
modules.tryIt: Train small language models on three contrasting data mixtures (100% web, 50/50 web-code, code-dense), benchmarking downstream reasoning accuracy.
modules.outcome: Formulate data mixture strategies, optimize domain proportions systematically, and deploy data annealing during pre-training cooldown.

modules.name: The Emergence Debate: Smooth Metrics vs. Step Discontinuities in Model Capabilities

objectives.text: - Review the historical literature on emergent abilities (Wei et al., 2022): the claim that certain capabilities appear abruptly and discontinuously at specific scales.
objectives.group: Emergent Abilities in Large Language Models

objectives.text: - Analyze the counter-argument (Schaeffer et al., 2023, "Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?"): emergence as an artifact of non-linear metrics.
objectives.group: Emergent Abilities in Large Language Models

objectives.text: - Compare discontinuous step-function metrics (accuracy, exact match) against continuous, smooth metrics (token cross-entropy loss, Brier score).
objectives.group: Emergent Abilities in Large Language Models

objectives.text: - Prove mathematically that a smooth, linear decrease in token error probability produces a sharp, non-linear step-function increase on multi-token sequence accuracy.
- Differentiate between genuine qualitative phase shifts (circuit formation, in-context learning emergence) versus measurement artifacts.
- Design rigorous evaluation protocols that report both smooth continuous metrics and discrete milestone accuracy to avoid deceptive claims.

modules.mentalModel: If you measure a student's knowledge using pass/fail on a 10-step math problem, a 10% skill increase looks like a sudden miracle; the underlying learning is continuous.
modules.tryIt: Simulate a model whose per-token error rate decreases linearly, plot the multi-token sequence accuracy curve, and demonstrate the mathematical illusion of emergence.
modules.outcome: Critically evaluate claims of emergent capabilities in foundation models, distinguish measurement artifacts, and report calibrated metrics.

modules.name: Tokenizer Science: Byte-Pair Encoding, Vocabulary Entropy & Cross-Lingual Compression

objectives.text: - Master the mathematics of Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE), WordPiece, and Unigram Language Model tokenization algorithms.
- Train tokenizers from scratch using Byte-Level BPE (Hugging Face Tokenizers) with custom normalization rules and regex pre-tokenization splits.
- Analyze the trade-offs of vocabulary size V: larger vocabularies increase embedding parameter count but improve sequence compression and inference speed.
- Measure tokenizer efficiency using bytes-per-token compression ratios and Shannon entropy across multilingual and code domains.
- Identify tokenization pathologies: arithmetic token fragmentation, capitalization sensitivity, and whitespace sensitivity in downstream reasoning.
- Evaluate the "fertility" metric: the average number of tokens required to represent a single word across low-resource languages, quantifying linguistic fairness.

modules.mentalModel: The tokenizer is the sensory organ of the language model; if numbers are chopped into arbitrary digit fragments, the model struggles with arithmetic.
modules.tryIt: Train a custom 32k vocabulary BPE tokenizer, calculate bytes-per-token compression ratios across code, English, and low-resource text, and analyze fertility.
modules.outcome: Build and evaluate custom tokenizers, analyze cross-lingual compression efficiency, and eliminate tokenization pathologies.

modules.name: Capstone Project: Compute-Optimal Scaling Curve Estimation & Loss Spike Diagnostics

objectives.text: - Train a grid of language models across 5 parameter scales (10M to 150M) and varying token budgets on an HPC cluster.

levels.title: Mechanistic Interpretability & Model Analysis
levels.scope: Master the scientific discipline of mechanistic interpretability: reverse-engineering neural network representations, probing internal latent spaces, circuit discovery (induction heads), disentangling superposition with Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), causal activation patching, and representation steering.
levels.prereqStated: Level 10 (Pre-Training Dynamics, Scaling Laws & Empirical Science)

modules.name: The Linear Representation Hypothesis & Latent Space Probing

objectives.text: - Formulate the Linear Representation Hypothesis (Park et al., Elhage et al.): high-level human concepts are encoded as linear directions in activation spaces.
- Implement linear diagnostic probes: train linear classifiers on intermediate hidden activations to predict semantic, syntactic, and factual properties.
- Control for probe memorization: compare linear probe accuracy against non-linear probes (MLPs) and randomized baseline controls (Hewitt & Liang selectivity).
- Analyze the geometric alignment of hidden representations across distinct layers, models, and training checkpoints.
- Implement Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) using linear and radial basis function (RBF) kernels to quantify representational similarity invariance.
- Use Singular Value Canonical Correlation Analysis (SVCCA) to isolate the intrinsic dimensionality of learned representations.

modules.mentalModel: The activation space of a neural network is a high-dimensional concept space; linear vectors act as geometric coordinates for abstract ideas.
modules.tryIt: Train a linear probe on the residual stream activations of a language model to extract grammatical tense, verifying high probe selectivity against random controls.
modules.outcome: Probe internal representations rigorously, test the linear representation hypothesis, and measure representational similarity using CKA.

modules.name: Circuit Discovery: Residual Stream Decomposition & Induction Head Identification

objectives.text: - Understand the Transformer as a residual stream communication channel where attention heads and MLPs write additive linear updates.
- Deconstruct the multi-head attention operation into independent QK (query-key addressing) and OV (output-value transformation) circuits (Elhage et al.).
- Trace information flow mathematically: compute direct, indirect, and mediated path contributions to the final vocabulary projection logits.
- Analyze the mechanistic discovery of induction heads (Olsson et al., 2022): two-head circuits that implement pattern completion [A][B] ... [A] -> [B].
- Write automated induction head detectors that measure attention score spikes on repeated random token sequences across all layer-head pairs.
- Trace the emergence of induction heads during pre-training: correlate their formation with the phase shift in in-context learning loss curves.

modules.mentalModel: Induction heads are the fundamental algorithmic microprocessors of in-context learning, copying historical patterns into future predictions.
modules.tryIt: Implement an automated induction head detection script in PyTorch/TransformerLens, scan a model, and identify the exact layer and head indices responsible.
modules.outcome: Decompose the Transformer residual stream into mathematical circuits and mechanically identify induction heads responsible for in-context learning.

modules.name: Disentangling Superposition: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) & Dictionary Learning

objectives.text: - Formulate the superposition hypothesis: neural networks represent more features than they have dimensions by packing non-orthogonal directions into activations.
- Understand polysemanticity: individual neurons activate for multiple unrelated semantic concepts, preventing clean single-neuron interpretation.
- Analyze the geometry of almost-orthogonal vectors in high dimensions bounded by the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma.
- Implement Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) with overcomplete hidden layers (e.g., 8x to 32x expansion) and L1 sparsity regularization penalties.
- Train an SAE on intermediate residual stream activations to disentangle superposed representations into thousands of sparse, monosemantic latent features.
- Evaluate SAE quality: compute the L0 sparsity norm (average active latents per token) and reconstruction loss percentage on downstream evaluation benchmarks.

modules.mentalModel: Superposition packs a crowded city into a small suitcase; an SAE unpacks the suitcase, giving every item its own dedicated hanger.
modules.tryIt: Train an SAE on hidden residual activations, evaluate L0 sparsity and reconstruction fidelity, and extract monosemantic feature interpretations.
modules.outcome: Disentangle polysemantic representations using Sparse Autoencoders, extract monosemantic feature dictionaries, and measure L0 sparsity.

modules.name: Causal Tracing & Activation Patching: Localizing Factual Recall

objectives.text: - Differentiate between passive observational correlation (probing) versus active causal intervention in neural network representations.
- Implement causal mediation analysis and activation patching (Meng et al., ROME): corrupting input embeddings with noise and restoring clean activations.
- Localize factual knowledge storage: identify specific early MLP layers and late attention heads that causally mediate factual subject-relation recall.
- Formulate Rank-One Model Editing (ROME) and MEMIT: computing optimal closed-form updates to MLP weight matrices to update specific factual associations.
- Measure the generalization and specificity of mechanistic model edits: verify that editing "Eiffel Tower -> Rome" does not corrupt general knowledge about Paris.
- Analyze the limitations of direct weight editing: unintended collateral damage, distortion of adjacent concepts, and catastrophic forgetting.

modules.mentalModel: Activation patching performs surgical neurosurgery on running neural networks to pinpoint the exact circuit that stores a specific memory.
modules.tryIt: Implement activation patching on a factual query ("The capital of France is [Paris]"), localizing the exact MLP layer that restores the clean output from noise.
modules.outcome: Execute causal activation patching to localize model capabilities and analyze direct weight editing mechanisms and limitations.

modules.name: Representation Engineering (RepE): Contrastive Activation Vectors & Steering

objectives.text: - Formalize Representation Engineering (RepE, Zou et al.): directly inspecting and manipulating the top-down cognitive states of models during generation.
- Extract concept direction vectors by computing contrastive activation differences across paired prompts (e.g., honest vs. dishonest, sycophantic vs. factual).
- Apply Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to contrastive activation sets to identify the principal axis of the target concept in the residual stream.
- Implement runtime activation steering: add or subtract the scaled concept vector v directly to the residual stream: h_l' = h_l + alpha * v.
- Compare activation steering with prompt engineering: evaluate robustness against adversarial prompt jailbreaks, token overhead, and stability over long contexts.
- Analyze the alignment tax of excessive steering: monitor the degradation of grammatical fluency and reasoning ability under high steering coefficients alpha.

modules.mentalModel: Prompting talks to the model through its ears; activation steering reaches directly into its brain to tilt its internal thought compass.
modules.tryIt: Extract a "truthfulness" concept vector from contrastive pairs, inject it during inference with varying alpha coefficients, and measure the reduction in hallucination.
modules.outcome: Extract contrastive concept vectors, steer model generation behavior directly at the latent representation level, and quantify steering trade-offs.

objectives.text: - Construct an automated mechanistic analysis harness in PyTorch (leveraging TransformerLens or native hooks) targeting a specific reasoning behavior.

modules.mentalModel: Rigorous mechanistic interpretability transforms the black box into a transparent, mathematically verifiable computing circuit.

levels.title: AI Alignment, Safety & Ethical Research
levels.scope: Master the mathematical derivations, empirical algorithms, and ethical methodologies of AI alignment: preference modeling (Bradley-Terry, RLHF, DPO, KTO), reward gaming and Goodhart's law, adversarial robustness (PGD, GCG attacks), algorithmic fairness audits, and AI safety governance frameworks.

modules.name: Preference Modeling Derivations: Bradley-Terry, RLHF & Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)

objectives.text: - Formalize human preference datasets D = {(x, y_w, y_l)} where y_w is the preferred completion and y_l is the dispreferred completion.
- Formulate the Bradley-Terry preference model: P(y_w \succ y_l | x) = \sigma(r(x, y_w) - r(x, y_l)).
- Train deep Reward Models (RMs) by minimizing the negative log-likelihood of pairwise preferences with margin regularizers.
- Analyze the classical RLHF pipeline (PPO with frozen reference policy KL penalties) and identify its complexity and training instability.
- Derive Direct Preference Optimization (DPO, Rafailov et al.) analytically: express the optimal reward implicitly as r(x, y) = \beta \log (\pi_\theta(y|x) / \pi_{ref}(y|x)).
- Implement the DPO loss objective without training an explicit reward model or sampling actions via reinforcement learning.

modules.mentalModel: DPO proves that an optimal policy implicitly defines its own reward function, turning unstable RLHF into stable binary cross-entropy optimization.
modules.tryIt: Derive the DPO loss gradient analytically with respect to model parameters, and implement the DPO loss function in PyTorch with numerical stability clamps.
modules.outcome: Derive and implement state-of-the-art preference optimization algorithms (Reward Modeling, RLHF, DPO, KTO) from first principles.

modules.name: Reward Over-Optimization, Sycophancy & Goodhart’s Law in Language Models

objectives.text: - Understand Goodhart’s Law in AI alignment: when a proxy reward model becomes the optimization target, it ceases to be a reliable measure of true quality.
- Quantify reward over-optimization: measure the divergence between proxy reward and true human preference as KL divergence from the base model increases.
- Analyze the "Alignment Tax": the degradation of mathematical reasoning, coding capability, or linguistic diversity resulting from aggressive preference tuning.
- Define sycophancy in aligned models: the tendency of language models to echo and validate false user assertions to maximize superficial agreeableness.
- Construct synthetic contrastive sycophancy datasets evaluating model adherence to factual truth when contradicted by authoritative user prompts.
- Mitigate sycophantic behavior using targeted preference tuning and negative activation steering in the residual stream.

modules.mentalModel: Optimizing aggressively against a proxy reward produces a model that flatters the rater rather than speaking the objective truth.
modules.tryIt: Evaluate an aligned model on a sycophancy probe dataset, measure the percentage of false user statements validated by the model, and implement a corrective DPO fine-tune.
modules.outcome: Diagnose and quantify reward over-optimization, measure the alignment tax, and eliminate sycophancy in preference-tuned models.

modules.name: Adversarial Robustness: Projected Gradient Descent (PGD), GCG Attacks & Red-Teaming

objectives.text: - Formulate adversarial perturbations as constrained optimization: \max_{||\delta|| \le \epsilon} L(\theta, x + \delta, y).
- Implement the Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) and multi-step Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) with projection back onto the L-infinity epsilon ball.
- Understand adversarial training (Madry et al.): formulating the min-max robust optimization game to learn robust representations.
- Master discrete adversarial optimization against aligned language models: Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG, Zou et al.) attack suffixes.
- Analyze universal adversarial triggers: transferability of adversarial suffix tokens across disparate open-source and proprietary foundation models.
- Structure systematic red-teaming methodologies: automated red-teaming with adversarial LLMs, threat modeling, and defense mechanisms (perplexity filtering).

modules.mentalModel: Adversarial attacks reveal the non-robust, brittle shortcuts learned by deep networks; robustness requires closing off unconstrained gradient directions.
modules.tryIt: Implement a PGD attack on a neural classifier in PyTorch, measure accuracy degradation, and verify robustness recovery through adversarial training.
modules.outcome: Formulate adversarial attacks, implement PGD and discrete token jailbreaks, and design defensive adversarial training protocols.

modules.name: Algorithmic Fairness: Demographic Parity, Equalized Odds & Auditing Disparities

objectives.text: - Formalize core fairness criteria: Demographic Parity (P(\hat{Y}=1 | A=0) = P(\hat{Y}=1 | A=1)), Equal Opportunity, and Equalized Odds.
- Prove the Impossibility Theorem of Fairness (Kleinberg et al.): Demographic Parity, Equalized Odds, and Predictive Parity cannot be satisfied simultaneously.
- Measure bias in natural language models: gender/racial bias in word embeddings (WEAT), stereotypical association tests, and disparate impact ratios.
- Categorize bias mitigation interventions: pre-processing (re-weighing, data re-sampling), in-processing (adversarial debiasing), and post-processing (threshold tuning).
- Conduct systematic algorithmic fairness audits on production models, quantifying performance disparities across sensitive intersectional demographic groups.
- Document algorithmic impact assessments and author comprehensive Model Cards (Mitchell et al.) detailing intended scope and fairness benchmarks.

modules.mentalModel: Fairness metrics mathematically conflict; an ethical researcher must explicitly choose and defend which fairness trade-off fits the domain.
modules.tryIt: Audit a predictive model for disparate impact across demographic subgroups, calculate Equalized Odds ratios, and implement an in-processing debiasing constraint.
modules.outcome: Apply mathematical definitions of algorithmic fairness, audit deep learning models for demographic disparities, and implement debiasing interventions.

modules.name: AI Governance & Research Ethics: Institutional Review Boards, Dual-Use & Safety Charters

objectives.text: - Navigate academic research ethics and Institutional Review Board (IRB) protocols for human-subject data collection and crowdsourced annotation.
- Evaluate dual-use hazards in AI research: autonomous cyber-offensive tooling, chemical/biological weapon synthesis risk, and automated disinformation pipelines.
- Apply the Menlo Report and Belmont Report principles (beneficence, justice, respect for persons) to AI/ML research methodologies.
- Establish responsible vulnerability disclosure protocols for newly discovered model jailbreaks, security bypasses, and data extraction vectors.
- Understand international AI regulatory frameworks (EU AI Act risk classifications, US Executive Orders, Frontier Model Safety Charters).
- Implement tiered model release strategies: gated access, safety evaluation milestones, and model weight watermarking.

modules.mentalModel: Cutting-edge scientific power brings severe societal responsibility; ethical researchers evaluate dual-use consequences before training begins.
modules.tryIt: Author a dual-use risk assessment and mitigation framework for a hypothetical frontier foundation model capability release.
modules.outcome: Navigate scientific research ethics, conduct dual-use risk assessments, and establish responsible disclosure and governance policies.

levels.title: Multimodal & Cross-Disciplinary AI for Science
levels.scope: Master the architectural principles of multimodal foundation models and cross-disciplinary AI for science: joint vision-language contrastive alignment (CLIP, SigLIP), cross-modal projectors (LLaVA), structural biology models (AlphaFold/ESM), physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), and neural operators.

modules.name: Cross-Modal Contrastive Alignment: CLIP, SigLIP & Dual-Encoder Geometry

objectives.text: - Formulate the dual-encoder contrastive learning objective: parallel image and text encoders projecting disparate modalities into a shared normalized embedding space.
- Derive the symmetric cross-entropy loss over image-to-text and text-to-image cosine similarities with a learned temperature parameter.
- Implement zero-shot classification via text prompt engineering ("a photo of a {class}") and vector similarity dot products.
- Analyze the communication bottleneck of standard CLIP: global multi-GPU All-Gather operations required for Softmax denominator normalization across large batch sizes.
- Formulate SigLIP (Zhai et al.): replacing multi-class Softmax with independent pairwise sigmoid losses over all image-text pairs.
- Implement SigLIP loss in PyTorch, proving linear communication scaling and improved zero-shot retrieval accuracy under identical batch budgets.

modules.mentalModel: Cross-modal contrastive learning constructs a shared semantic Rosetta Stone where visual concepts and linguistic symbols map to identical coordinates.
modules.tryIt: Implement the SigLIP pairwise sigmoid loss function from scratch, and verify that it avoids global cross-GPU All-Gather operations.
modules.outcome: Build, train, and optimize dual-encoder multimodal contrastive models and understand the geometric alignment of cross-modal spaces.

modules.name: Vision-Language Projection Architectures: LLaVA, Cross-Attention & Perceiver Resamplers

objectives.text: - Process continuous 2D images as discrete token sequences using Vision Transformers (ViT): patch extraction, linear projection, and class token embeddings.
- Implement linear and multi-layer perceptron (MLP) projection adapters (LLaVA architecture) mapping frozen vision tokens directly into the LLM token embedding space.
- Analyze the information density mismatch: high-resolution image patches yield hundreds of tokens, necessitating spatial pooling or token pruning.
- Implement Perceiver Resamplers (Flamingo architecture) using a fixed set of learnable latent queries to cross-attend into arbitrary-length visual sequences.
- Master gated cross-attention layers inserted between frozen language layers, allowing visual signals to steer language generation without catastrophic forgetting.
- Evaluate multimodal reasoning: visual question answering (VQA), chart comprehension, and document understanding across standard multimodal benchmarks.

modules.mentalModel: The projection adapter acts as an optical cable, translating high-dimensional visual feature vectors into tokens the language model's residual stream can parse.
modules.tryIt: Build a minimal LLaVA-style multimodal model in PyTorch combining a frozen ViT encoder, a 2-layer projection MLP, and a small language model.
modules.outcome: Architect multimodal vision-language models, implement projection adapters and Perceiver resamplers, and benchmark multimodal reasoning.

modules.name: AI for Structural Biology & Molecular Modeling: AlphaFold & ESM Principles

objectives.text: - Represent biological sequences (DNA, RNA, proteins) as discrete token sequences over amino acid alphabets.
- Master evolutionary scale modeling (ESM, Rives et al.): training massive masked language models on billions of natural protein sequences to learn evolutionary fitness.
- Extract learned attention contact maps from protein language models, proving that self-attention weights directly reflect 3D residue-residue physical proximity.
- Understand the structural biology challenge: predicting 3D atomic coordinates (x, y, z) from 1D primary amino acid sequences.
- Master the invariant point attention (IPA) mechanism in AlphaFold2: operating directly on 3D Euclidean frame transformations (SE(3) equivariance).
- Interpret confidence metrics in structural biology: predicted Local Distance Difference Test (pLDDT) and Predicted Aligned Error (PAE) matrices.

modules.mentalModel: Biological evolution acts as nature's unsupervised pre-training; language models trained on sequences recover 3D biophysical structure.
modules.tryIt: Load a pre-trained protein language model (ESM-2), extract the attention contact matrix for a target sequence, and compare against experimental PDB structures.
modules.outcome: Master the foundations of biological AI models, extract structural contact maps from protein representations, and evaluate 3D structural predictions.

modules.name: Physics-Informed Machine Learning: PINNs, Operator Learning & Conservation Laws

objectives.text: - Formulate partial differential equations (PDEs) as loss regularizers: Burgers' equation, Navier-Stokes, and heat diffusion.
- Implement Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs, Raissi et al.): using autograd to compute exact spatial and temporal derivatives (du/dt, d^2u/dx^2).
- Minimize the PDE residual loss L_residual = ||f(x, t; u)||^2 alongside empirical initial and boundary condition losses without requiring mesh generation.
- Understand the limitation of standard PINNs: learning a single specific PDE solution rather than learning the general solution operator across arbitrary input fields.
- Formulate Neural Operators (Li et al.): learning mappings between infinite-dimensional function spaces invariant to mesh discretization.
- Implement Fourier Neural Operators (FNO): computing convolutions in Fourier space via Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT) for hyper-fast fluid simulation.

modules.mentalModel: Standard ML fits curves to scattered data points; Physics-Informed ML constrains the curve to strictly satisfy the fundamental differential laws of the universe.
modules.tryIt: Implement a Physics-Informed Neural Network in PyTorch solving the 1D wave equation, computing exact second-order derivatives via autograd.
modules.outcome: Implement Physics-Informed Neural Networks, enforce physical conservation laws in loss functions, and master Fourier Neural Operators.

modules.name: Cross-Domain Transfer Learning: Adapting Foundation Models to Scientific Disciplines

objectives.text: - Adapt general foundation models to specialized scientific domains (medicine, climate modeling, chemistry, genomics) via continued domain pre-training.
- Prevent catastrophic forgetting of general reasoning: blend domain-specific scientific corpora with 10-20% general instruction and math replay data.
- Manage vocabulary adaptation: extending tokenizers with scientific nomenclature (SMILES chemical strings, genomic k-mers) without corrupting base embeddings.
- Design domain-specific validation suites evaluating both statistical performance and physical plausibility (e.g., mass conservation, charge neutrality).
- Conduct blinded expert evaluations with domain specialists (chemists, biologists, clinicians) to evaluate real-world utility beyond academic benchmarks.
- Document scientific reproducibility artifacts: raw simulation data, random seeds, environmental parameters, and verified software container recipes.

modules.mentalModel: Adapting a foundation model to science is not just teaching it vocabulary; it is teaching it to respect the non-negotiable invariants of physical reality.
modules.tryIt: Fine-tune a foundation model on a domain-specific scientific corpus with replay data, and verify that general reasoning benchmarks do not degrade.
modules.outcome: Adapt foundation models to complex scientific domains, prevent catastrophic forgetting, and enforce domain-specific physical invariants.

modules.name: Flagship Project 1: Rigorous Reproduction of a Top-Tier Conference Paper

objectives.text: Select a seminal, highly cited paper published within the last 24 months in a top-tier machine learning conference (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR).
Re-implement the core model architecture, custom loss functions, and data preprocessing pipelines from scratch in PyTorch without copying official source code.
Execute the full experimental training suite under strictly identical hyperparameter budgets, hardware settings, and random seeds.
Identify unstated implementation tricks, missing mathematical assumptions, or discrepancies between reported paper metrics and empirical reproduction results.
Perform an ablation study evaluating the sensitivity of the reproduced method to learning rate schedules, seed variation, and batch size scaling.
Author a formal scientific reproduction report adhering to the NeurIPS Reproducibility Challenge guidelines, complete with verified code release.

modules.outcome: A scientifically verified reproduction codebase and comprehensive artifact report validating or disputing published claims.

modules.name: Flagship Project 2: Novel Sequence Architecture with Empirical Scaling Analysis

objectives.text: Design and implement an innovative sequence modeling architecture uniting sub-quadratic State Space Models (Mamba) with local self-attention mechanisms.
Derive the analytical time and memory complexity of the proposed hybrid architecture, proving linear or near-linear scaling with sequence length.
Pre-train a family of models across multiple compute budgets (10M to 250M parameters) on standardized multi-domain text corpora on an HPC cluster.
Fit empirical Chinchilla scaling laws to quantify compute-optimal parameter and token allocations for the proposed hybrid architecture.
Evaluate associative recall and long-context reasoning using synthetic needle-in-a-haystack and real-world long-context document understanding benchmarks.
Profile hardware execution: measure Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU), peak VRAM consumption, and wall-clock inference latency up to 64k tokens.

modules.outcome: A novel, fully benchmarked sequence model architecture accompanied by empirical scaling curves and compute efficiency analyses.

modules.name: Flagship Project 3: Decontaminated Domain Benchmark with Human Agreement Calibration

objectives.text: Curate a novel, multi-task domain-specific evaluation benchmark dataset comprising at least 500 challenging multi-step reasoning instances.
Author a rigorous annotation codebook, conduct multi-annotator human evaluation, and verify statistical reliability (Krippendorff’s alpha > 0.80).
Build an automated 13-gram contamination detection scanner using suffix arrays to verify zero overlap with standard open-source pre-training corpora.
Evaluate a comprehensive suite of proprietary and open-source foundation models under standardized zero-shot and few-shot prompting conditions.
Implement a bidirectional LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline, calibrating automated scores against human expert consensus via Kendall’s tau and Spearman rank correlation.
Format all dataset artifacts with Datasheets for Datasets documentation and release clean evaluation harnesses on Hugging Face Datasets.

modules.outcome: A pristine, decontaminated domain benchmark established as an open-source evaluation standard for the research community.

modules.name: Flagship Project 4: Mechanistic Circuit Investigation & Steering in Frontier LLMs

objectives.text: Select a complex, non-trivial capability in an open-weight foundation model (e.g., indirect object identification, counterfactual reasoning, or sycophancy).
Apply causal activation patching across all layers and token positions to map the exact minimal computational circuit mediating the target capability.
Deconstruct mediating attention heads into mathematically formulated QK addressing circuits and OV information-routing circuits.
Train an overcomplete Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) with L1 regularization on the critical bottleneck layer, extracting monosemantic feature dictionaries.
Extract contrastive activation steering vectors and demonstrate targeted behavioral steering during generation without degrading general language perplexity.
Author an interactive research report featuring causal circuit wiring diagrams, activation heatmaps, and mechanistic ablation proofs.

modules.outcome: An end-to-end mechanistic interpretability discovery identifying the internal computational circuit and demonstrating precise latent steering.

modules.name: Flagship Project 5: Continuous Flow Matching Diffusion Model for Scientific Modalities

objectives.text: Formulate and implement a continuous-time Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching (OT-CFM) generative model on a complex scientific modality.
Implement a modern Diffusion Transformer (DiT) velocity backbone with adaptive layer normalization conditioning and classifier-free guidance.
Construct straight-line probability paths between standard Gaussian priors and complex empirical data manifolds.
Implement accelerated adaptive ODE numerical solvers (Runge-Kutta 4, midpoint) achieving high-fidelity generation in 15 to 25 steps.
Evaluate generative distribution quality rigorously using clean Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Precision, Recall, and trajectory curvature metrics.
Benchmark generation speed, kinetic energy dissipation, and sample diversity against classical DDPM and score-based SDE baselines.

modules.outcome: A state-of-the-art continuous flow matching framework with publication-quality distribution metrics and accelerated numerical sampling.

modules.name: Flagship Project 6: Preference Optimization Regularization with Spectral Analysis

objectives.text: Formulate a novel regularization objective for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) that penalizes rank collapse in the weight update matrix Delta W.
Implement the spectral regularization algorithm in PyTorch, applying low-rank Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) constraints during preference tuning.
Train a foundation model on challenging conversational preference datasets, monitoring implicit reward margins and policy KL divergence.
Audit downstream performance: evaluate retention of mathematical reasoning, coding abilities, and factual truthfulness, quantifying the alignment tax.
Perform singular value spectral decomposition on weight deltas to verify that foundational pre-trained feature representations remain uncorrupted.
Conduct red-teaming audits to prove enhanced resistance to reward hacking, sycophancy, and adversarial jailbreak perturbations.

modules.outcome: A novel preference optimization methodology published with mathematical derivations, empirical proofs, and spectral analysis.
